jobs.title: Commissioning Program Manager, Infrastructure Delivery
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the physical infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale.

The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. As the portfolio grows, the team is building common standards, processes, tools, and reporting systems that allow commissioning programs to operate consistently across projects while giving teams and leadership clear visibility into readiness, risk, and execution.

About the Role

We are seeking a Commissioning Program Manager to build and scale the operating systems behind OpenAI’s infrastructure commissioning programs.

You will own the development and continuous improvement of commissioning standards, processes, tools, dashboards, and KPIs across the infrastructure portfolio. You will work closely with commissioning and construction teams to translate field execution needs into practical playbooks, workflows, templates, metrics, and reporting mechanisms that teams can use from construction readiness through testing and turnover.

This role sits at the intersection of infrastructure delivery, program management, process design, and data. The ideal candidate understands how complex construction projects operate and can turn fragmented workflows and project data into repeatable systems that improve execution without creating unnecessary administrative burden.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain commissioning program standards, playbooks, process maps, templates, checklists, stage gates, and acceptance criteria across infrastructure projects.

  • Establish consistent workflows for commissioning planning, construction readiness, QA/QC, issue management, document control, testing evidence, turnover, and lessons learned.

  • Define and maintain commissioning KPIs, dashboards, and scorecards that provide visibility into readiness, inspection completion, deficiencies, test progress, data quality, and turnover health.

  • Own requirements and operating workflows across commissioning trackers, construction management platforms, QA/QC systems, spreadsheets, and business intelligence tools.

  • Partner closely with commissioning and construction leads to translate field execution needs into practical processes and tools that can scale across projects.

  • Monitor adoption, data quality, and effectiveness of commissioning standards and tools; identify gaps and drive improvements as project and portfolio needs evolve.

  • Establish reporting cadences and develop executive-ready reporting that clearly communicates commissioning health, trends, blockers, risks, and decisions required.

  • Pilot new standards, processes, metrics, and tools on active projects, incorporate field feedback, and scale successful approaches across the infrastructure portfolio.

  • Partner with data, analytics, and tooling teams to improve automation, source-of-truth alignment, data integrity, and reporting reliability.

  • Drive continuous improvement by capturing lessons learned from project execution and incorporating them into future commissioning standards, workflows, dashboards, and KPIs.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in program management, project management, construction management, engineering, commissioning, facilities, project controls, or infrastructure delivery.

  • Hands-on experience working in construction or complex infrastructure environments, with an understanding of how field work is planned, coordinated, tracked, documented, tested, and turned over.

  • Experience developing or improving program standards, SOPs, process maps, playbooks, templates, trackers, stage gates, or operating rhythms used by project teams.

  • Strong comfort with data, metrics, dashboards, and reporting, including the ability to define meaningful KPIs, identify data-quality issues, and translate project information into actionable insights.

  • Working knowledge of commissioning, QA/QC, inspections, deficiency management, testing documentation, readiness reviews, or turnover processes; direct commissioning experience is strongly preferred.

  • Experience with construction, commissioning, project management, or analytics platforms such as Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, CxAlloy, Bluebeam, Smartsheet, Excel or Google Sheets, Looker, Tableau, Power BI, or similar tools.

  • Strong systems thinking with the ability to simplify complex workflows, establish clear ownership, and design processes that work for both field teams and program leadership.

  • Demonstrated ability to drive process and tooling adoption across multidisciplinary stakeholders without relying on formal authority.

  • Experience building dashboards, scorecards, KPI frameworks, or reporting systems for construction, commissioning, project controls, infrastructure operations, or PMO organizations is preferred.

  • Experience with mission-critical infrastructure, data centers, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, laboratories, or other complex technical facilities is preferred; PMP, Lean/Six Sigma, CxA, QCxP, or related credentials are a plus.

Location

This role is based in the San Francisco office or at an OpenAI self-build data center campus and is not a remote position.

Periodic travel to project sites is expected to develop a direct understanding of construction and commissioning workflows, support project teams, and ensure program standards and tools reflect field execution needs. Travel is expected to be less than 20%.

jobs.title: Commissioning Project Lead, Data Center Delivery
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building the infrastructure required to support the next generation of frontier AI systems. Through a combination of strategic partnerships and self-built data center campuses, we are scaling the power, cooling, electrical, mechanical, and controls infrastructure needed to deliver compute at unprecedented scale.

The Commissioning organization is responsible for ensuring this infrastructure is safely tested, validated, integrated, and transitioned into reliable operations. For our self-build campuses, the team operates through a hybrid delivery model: OpenAI provides commissioning leadership, discipline ownership, governance, and project integration, while commissioning partners provide field and test engineering capacity to support inspections, startup, testing, and turnover.

About the Role

We are seeking a Commissioning Project Lead to own the commissioning strategy and execution for a large-scale, self-build data center project.

You will lead the overall commissioning program from early construction planning through startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and final turnover. You will establish the commissioning execution plan, integrate commissioning activities into the master project schedule, coordinate multidisciplinary readiness, and lead the vendor commissioning partners providing field and test engineering capacity.

This role serves as the primary commissioning interface to project leadership, construction management, contractors, equipment vendors, operations, and commissioning partners. You will be responsible for creating clarity across organizations, identifying readiness and schedule risks early, and ensuring the facility progresses through testing and turnover against clearly defined acceptance criteria.

The role will initially support planning and coordination in a hybrid capacity and transition to full-time onsite presence as construction, inspections, startup, testing, and turnover become active.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the project commissioning strategy and execution plan, including scope, governance, acceptance criteria, responsibilities, sequencing, and escalation paths.

  • Lead the hybrid OpenAI and commissioning-partner delivery model, establishing clear RACI ownership, staffing requirements, performance expectations, and issue-management processes.

  • Integrate commissioning into the master project schedule, including construction readiness, energization, equipment startup, functional testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover milestones.

  • Lead commissioning coordination across construction management, contractors, design teams, equipment vendors, operations stakeholders, and field/test engineering teams.

  • Drive multidisciplinary commissioning readiness across electrical, mechanical, controls, and supporting infrastructure, identifying dependencies and resolving blockers before they affect testing.

  • Own visibility into commissioning risks, including schedule constraints, readiness gaps, design and submittal issues, safety constraints, resource bottlenecks, deficiencies, and documentation quality.

  • Review commissioning plans, test procedures, readiness checklists, deficiency logs, test reports, turnover packages, and other commissioning deliverables against established acceptance criteria.

  • Provide clear project and executive reporting on commissioning readiness, staffing, test progress, open risks, issue aging, and turnover status.

  • Drive final system acceptance, turnover readiness, closeout, and lessons learned to support a reliable transition from construction into operations.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in commissioning, construction, engineering, technical program management, or project delivery for mission-critical facilities or similarly complex technical infrastructure.

  • Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary commissioning programs through construction readiness, startup, functional performance testing, integrated systems testing, and turnover.

  • Strong working knowledge of electrical and mechanical commissioning workflows, with the ability to coordinate dependencies across power, cooling, controls, and supporting systems.

  • Experience integrating commissioning activities into construction schedules, lookaheads, energization plans, equipment startup sequences, and turnover milestones.

  • Strong owner, contractor, equipment vendor, and commissioning-agent management skills, including the ability to drive accountability across organizations without direct authority.

  • Experience managing commissioning documentation, test procedures, deficiency resolution, issue tracking, acceptance criteria, and quality governance.

  • Ability to identify commissioning and operational-readiness risks early and translate technical issues into actionable schedule and project decisions.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating technical readiness, risk, and recovery plans to senior project leadership.

  • Owner-side commissioning experience and experience establishing or scaling hybrid owner/vendor commissioning delivery models are strongly preferred.

  • Professional credentials such as a PE license, QCxP, CxA, BCxP, CCP, PMP, or other relevant commissioning, engineering, construction, or project management certification are preferred.

Location

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

Our Communications team includes External Communications, Internal Communications, and other strategic communications functions. This team’s ethos is to support OpenAI's mission and goals by clearly and authentically explaining our technology, values, and approach to safely building powerful AI.

About the Role

We’re looking for a senior communications leader to shape how OpenAI communicates about its emerging ads and monetization business.

This person will define the global narrative, lead communications for major product and business milestones, and build sustained programs that explain our approach to ads and monetization clearly and credibly. The role will be central to showing how OpenAI can develop advertising experiences that are useful to people, valuable to businesses, transparent in how they work and consistent with our mission.

You will work closely with Product, Go-to-Market, Marketing, Policy, Legal and Partnerships to anticipate opportunities and risks, develop integrated campaigns and help the business scale with trust. You will also serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on positioning, reputation, media strategy and the broader industry conversation.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role. The right person will be comfortable defining a long-term communications strategy, building the systems and relationships needed to execute it, and personally leading through high-profile launches and fast-moving issues.

This role reports to the VP of Communications and is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of four days per week in the office and offer relocation assistance


In this role, you will:

  • Define and lead communications strategy for OpenAI’s ads and monetization initiatives, from global narrative development through launches and sustained storytelling.

  • Build a clear, differentiated story about how OpenAI approaches ads, including the value it creates for users, businesses and the broader ecosystem.

  • Partner closely with Product, GTM and Marketing to deliver coordinated campaigns across earned, owned, and social channels in support of business outcomes.

  • Own media engagement and build trusted relationships with leading business, technology and advertising press.

  • Advise senior leadership on positioning, messaging, launch strategy, and how to proactively shape industry conversations.

  • Translate complex product, technical and commercial decisions into clear, accessible communications for a range of audiences.

  • Establish messaging, operating rhythms and communications systems that keep teams aligned as the business grows.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 12+ years of communications experience, with deep experience in ads and monetization at a high-growth technology company.

  • Strong press instincts and relationships, with a track record of shaping narratives and landing impactful coverage with business and industry media.

  • Demonstrate exceptional editorial judgment and taste.

  • Skilled at advising senior executives and navigating high-visibility environments with calm and clarity.

  • Can move fluidly between setting a strategic vision and executing the details.

  • Experience working in highly cross-functional, matrixed organizations, with strong instincts for alignment across product, GTM, and marketing.

  • Highly collaborative leader who can align diverse stakeholders behind a unified story.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital partners, is embarking on a journey to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure ecosystem. The Industrial Compute team is central to this mission, setting the core infra strategy and implementing this vision. From site selection to the buildout process, this team sits at the intersection of commercial, technical, strategy, and operations, interacting with teams and executives inside and outside of OpenAI.

About the Role

The Community Engagement Lead will be the primary bridge between OpenAI and the communities in Ohio. This role ensures that OpenAI builds strong, trust-based relationships with local stakeholders, communicates proactively about our projects, and integrates community priorities into our development approach. The role spans engagement, communications, and reputation management, and will partner closely with the Economic Development and Environmental leads.

Location: Portsmouth, Ohio or Southern Ohio

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain relationships with local leaders, community organizations, NGOs, and residents.

  • Develop and execute community engagement strategies for new and existing sites.

  • Represent OpenAI in public forums, hearings, and community events.

  • Partner with the Economic Development Lead on incentive compliance and community benefits.

  • Partner with the Environmental Lead on communicating environmental stewardship and sustainability efforts.

  • Develop proactive communications to address concerns, highlight benefits, and reduce risk of opposition.

  • Monitor community sentiment and advise executives on risks and opportunities.

  • Create a community engagement playbook that can scale across geographies.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years in community affairs, public engagement, or corporate communications.

  • Proven track record engaging diverse community stakeholders for large infrastructure or technology projects.

  • Strong public speaking and facilitation skills.

  • Ability to manage sensitive political and reputational issues.

  • Experience integrating community benefits (workforce, education, infrastructure support) into development strategies.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI's Compensation team plays a crucial role in rewarding and retaining world-class talent who will ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. By crafting and implementing innovative compensation strategies, we ensure our compensation offerings are competitive, equitable, and aligned with OpenAI's mission to scale intelligently and ethically.

About the Role

We are expanding our Compensation team and seeking a Compensation Business Partner to help build the compensation pillar for our go-to-market organization. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for someone who brings deep GTM compensation expertise and enjoys turning evolving business needs into practical, scalable programs.

As a member of the total rewards team, you will partner closely with GTM leaders, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, Finance, and other cross-functional teams. You will spearhead compensation work across benchmarking, offer review, program design, and job architecture, with particular focus on the needs of a rapidly growing commercial organization.

The shape of the work will evolve as the business grows. At times, you may independently lead key initiatives from strategy through execution. At other times, you will work alongside additional compensation partners and cross-functional resources. Success in this role requires comfort operating with ambiguity, strong judgment, and a willingness to stay close to the details while building for scale.

This is an individual contributor role, designed for a subject-matter expert and hands-on builder.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and evolve compensation programs that support OpenAI’s growing GTM organization.

  • Serve as a trusted compensation advisor to GTM leaders, HR Business Partners, Recruiting, and Finance.

  • Lead compensation analysis and approval for offers, balancing market context, internal consistency, and OpenAI’s compensation philosophy.

  • Own benchmarking and market analysis for GTM roles, translating insights into clear recommendations and scalable practices.

  • Partner on the design and optimization of sales compensation programs, job architecture, and related compensation frameworks.

  • Develop approaches that can flex with changing business priorities, organizational growth, and new talent needs.

  • Move fluidly between strategic design and hands-on execution, including building processes and operating mechanisms where they do not yet exist.

  • Collaborate with the broader Compensation team to share insights and strengthen company-wide programs.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 6+ years of compensation experience, including meaningful depth supporting GTM or commercial organizations.

  • Strong expertise in sales compensation, GTM benchmarking, and compensation program design.

  • Experience building or materially evolving compensation programs in a fast-growing, dynamic organization.

  • A builder mindset: you are energized by ambiguity and comfortable creating structure as the business evolves.

  • Strong analytical judgment and the ability to translate complex data into practical recommendations.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trust with senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners.

  • The ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a broader team.

  • Experience with job architecture is strongly preferred.

Location and Workplace

This role is based in our New York or San Francisco office and we aren’t considering remote applications at this time. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays. We also offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Our open-plan offices have height-adjustable desks, conference rooms, phone booths, well-stocked kitchens full of snacks and drinks, three in-house prepared meals daily, outdoor space for working and socializing, wellness rooms, private bike storage, and more.

jobs.title: Compensation Programs & Operations Lead
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Compensation team helps attract, reward, and retain the people advancing our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. We develop compensation strategies and programs that support a rapidly evolving business, combining market insight, sound judgment, and thoughtful execution. We partner across People, Finance, Legal, and the business to deliver programs that employees and leaders can understand and trust.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Compensation Programs & Operations Lead to own the end-to-end program management of our cyclical and ad hoc compensation programs globally. You will turn compensation priorities into executable plans and lead delivery from initial scoping through launch, reconciliation, and continuous improvement.

This is a senior, hands-on role for a compensation subject-matter expert who is energized by operations and E2E program ownership. You should bring experience across compensation operations analysis, compensation analysis, business partnership, and program management. Having done this work yourself, you understand the practical details behind compensation decisions and what it takes to implement them accurately.

You will establish how our compensation programs run: the calendar, responsibilities, systems requirements, controls, communications, and handoffs that connect program design to the employee experience. You’ll partner closely with Compensation Partners, HR Business Partners, People Operations, People Technology, Finance, Payroll, Equity Administration, and Legal, creating clarity and driving execution as priorities evolve.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead our compensation program portfolio. Own the integrated roadmap and calendar for cyclical and ad hoc programs, including compensation reviews, bonus and equity cycles, promotion-related compensation processes, recognition and retention initiatives, and new program launches.

  • Drive programs from planning through completion. Define scope, deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, and resource needs. Coordinate work across teams, resolve blockers, and bring decisions and tradeoffs to the right owners early.

  • Translate compensation expertise into practical operations. Work with Compensation Partners and program owners to turn approved designs into clear eligibility rules, calculations, workflows, approval paths, and exception processes. Identify gaps and implementation risks before launch.

  • Stay close to the analysis and data. Build and review models, validate inputs and calculations, investigate discrepancies, and reconcile final outcomes. Be comfortable working directly in the details when a program needs it.

  • Build reliable execution controls. Establish quality checks, documented approvals, access controls, and audit trails. Coordinate accurate handoffs to Payroll, Equity Administration, and People Operations, with clear ownership through completion.

  • Shape compensation systems and tooling. Translate business needs into requirements, partner with People Technology on configuration and integrations, lead user acceptance testing, and prioritize improvements that reduce manual work and errors.

  • Manage incoming requests and changing priorities. Create a practical intake and prioritization process for ad hoc compensation initiatives. Make capacity, timing, and dependencies visible so urgent work can be delivered alongside recurring commitments.

  • Make programs easier to understand and use. Develop operating guides, manager resources, communications, and training. Equip Compensation Partners and other stakeholders to explain programs consistently and resolve questions efficiently.

  • Improve how the function operates. Measure accuracy, timeliness, manual effort, and stakeholder experience. Run post-cycle reviews and turn findings into simpler processes, stronger documentation, and effective automation.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of progressive compensation experience, including substantial responsibility for global compensation programs and operations in a complex, fast-growing organization.

  • Have performed the core responsibilities of a Compensation Operations Analyst, Compensation Analyst, Compensation Partner, and Compensation Program Manager, whether through separate roles or a combination of positions.

  • Bring deep compensation expertise across base pay, incentives, equity, market benchmarking, salary structures, and job architecture, and understand how these elements translate into day-to-day administration.

  • Have independently led complex compensation cycles and new initiatives, coordinating multiple teams from planning and analysis through implementation and reconciliation.

  • Are deliberately drawn to an operations-focused role. You enjoy making programs work, improving the details, and building processes that others can rely on.

  • Combine strong analytical skills with practical systems experience, including advanced spreadsheet modeling and hands-on work with Workday or comparable HR and compensation platforms.

  • Can establish priorities and drive progress when requirements are incomplete or changing, while making thoughtful tradeoffs about speed, accuracy, and capacity.

  • Communicate clearly with senior leaders and working teams, influence across functions, and make ownership and next steps explicit.

  • Exercise sound judgment with confidential information and bring a high standard of accuracy, accountability, and service to your work.

jobs.title: Component and Product Quality Engineer, Interconnects
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

OpenAI's Hardware organization builds supercompute platforms from silicon and boards to full rack-scale systems to power advanced AI workloads. This role owns end-to-end quality for high-speed interconnect hardware across the product lifecycle: early design influence, supplier/contract manufacturer readiness, qualification, ramp, and fleet quality in lab and data center environments.

You will be the quality lead for advanced interconnect components and assemblies, including high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges, patch panels, backplane/cable-backplane solutions, high-speed connectors, and related electro-mechanical interfaces. You will partner closely with electrical, mechanical, SI/PI, systems, reliability, operations, and external vendors to prevent escapes and drive rapid, data-driven containment and corrective action.

In this role you will:

  • Own quality for advanced interconnect components and assemblies: high-speed connectors, high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges (e.g., cable cassette style assemblies), patch panels & optics, and backplane/cable-backplane interconnect solutions.

  • Drive quality-by-design: participate in design reviews, DFM/DFx, tolerance stacks, material and plating selections, connector mating strategy, strain relief, and assembly methods to reduce variation and field failures.

  • Define and track quality and reliability metrics (DPPM, yield, escapes, RMA/FRACAS trends, Cpk/Ppk where applicable) for interconnects across NPI and mass production.

  • Build and execute qualification strategies for cables/connectors/patch panels (mechanical, environmental, electrical, and reliability), including test coverage, sample plans, clear pass/fail criteria, defining installation criteria and processes, optics termination quality management and setting fiber standards criteria.

  • Partner with engineering and operations to drive smooth ramp: risk assessments, pilot build learnings, change control, and readiness reviews (EVT/DVT/PVT/MP or equivalent phases).

  • Own supplier and CM performance management: scorecards, audits (process and quality system), and follow-up to close findings with verified effectiveness

  • Work with suppliers to improve manufacturing throughput, stability, and yields for cable and connector assembly processes (e.g., wire prep, welding/crimping, overmolding/injection molding, plating, and assembly fixturing).

  • Lead rapid containment and root-cause investigations for failures found during bring-up, system integration tests, reliability testing, and fleet deployments.

  • Own the end-to-end corrective action process (8D, 5-Whys, Ishikawa, DOE as needed): define problem statements, isolate variables, validate root cause, implement fixes, and verify effectiveness.

  • Partner with SI/PI and test teams to correlate electrical performance issues (e.g., link margin, BER, eye closure, impedance discontinuities, PAM4, TDR and VNA) with manufacturing and mechanical drivers (connector wear, plating, contamination, misalignment, cable routing, assembly variation).

  • Support integration and deployment of OpenAI supercompute racks in lab and data center environments; identify quality risks tied to shipping, handling, installation, and service operations.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • 7+ years of experience in quality engineering, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or reliability for interconnects or high-speed hardware used in servers, networking, storage, or high-performance compute systems.

  • Hands-on experience with high-speed copper interconnect products: connectors and/or cable assemblies; familiarity with patch panels or backplane/cable-backplane solutions is a plus

  • Strong command of problem-solving and quality tools: 8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone, PFMEA/control plans, SPC/MSA (gauge R&R), and change control.

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, GD&T basics, and electrical/interface specifications; comfortable working across ME/EE/SI disciplines.

  • Experience driving supplier/CM improvements (audits, scorecards, CAPA) and managing nonconformance/MRB workflows.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to drive alignment across internal teams and external partners.

  • Experience with cable manufacturing and assembly processes (wire treatment, resistance welding/laser welding, crimping, overmolding/injection molding, braiding/shielding, plating, and automated test).

  • Experience with optical interconnects (AOC/DAC, pluggable modules such as QSFP/OSFP), fiber termination quality, optical return loss, end-face inspection standards (IEC 61300), and contamination control practices.

  • Ability to travel internationally and work effectively across time zones with ODM/JDM and supplier partners.

jobs.description_plain: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform. About the Role OpenAI's Hardware organization builds supercompute platforms from silicon and boards to full rack-scale systems to power advanced AI workloads. This role owns end-to-end quality for high-speed interconnect hardware across the product lifecycle: early design influence, supplier/contract manufacturer readiness, qualification, ramp, and fleet quality in lab and data center environments. You will be the quality lead for advanced interconnect components and assemblies, including high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges, patch panels, backplane/cable-backplane solutions, high-speed connectors, and related electro-mechanical interfaces. You will partner closely with electrical, mechanical, SI/PI, systems, reliability, operations, and external vendors to prevent escapes and drive rapid, data-driven containment and corrective action. In this role you will: - Own quality for advanced interconnect components and assemblies: high-speed connectors, high-speed copper cables, cable cartridges (e.g., cable cassette style assemblies), patch panels & optics, and backplane/cable-backplane interconnect solutions. - Drive quality-by-design: participate in design reviews, DFM/DFx, tolerance stacks, material and plating selections, connector mating strategy, strain relief, and assembly methods to reduce variation and field failures. - Define and track quality and reliability metrics (DPPM, yield, escapes, RMA/FRACAS trends, Cpk/Ppk where applicable) for interconnects across NPI and mass production. - Build and execute qualification strategies for cables/connectors/patch panels (mechanical, environmental, electrical, and reliability), including test coverage, sample plans, clear pass/fail criteria, defining installation criteria and processes, optics termination quality management and setting fiber standards criteria. - Partner with engineering and operations to drive smooth ramp: risk assessments, pilot build learnings, change control, and readiness reviews (EVT/DVT/PVT/MP or equivalent phases). - Own supplier and CM performance management: scorecards, audits (process and quality system), and follow-up to close findings with verified effectiveness - Work with suppliers to improve manufacturing throughput, stability, and yields for cable and connector assembly processes (e.g., wire prep, welding/crimping, overmolding/injection molding, plating, and assembly fixturing). - Lead rapid containment and root-cause investigations for failures found during bring-up, system integration tests, reliability testing, and fleet deployments. - Own the end-to-end corrective action process (8D, 5-Whys, Ishikawa, DOE as needed): define problem statements, isolate variables, validate root cause, implement fixes, and verify effectiveness. - Partner with SI/PI and test teams to correlate electrical performance issues (e.g., link margin, BER, eye closure, impedance discontinuities, PAM4, TDR and VNA) with manufacturing and mechanical drivers (connector wear, plating, contamination, misalignment, cable routing, assembly variation). - Support integration and deployment of OpenAI supercompute racks in lab and data center environments; identify quality risks tied to shipping, handling, installation, and service operations. You might thrive in this role if you: - 7+ years of experience in quality engineering, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or reliability for interconnects or high-speed hardware used in servers, networking, storage, or high-performance compute systems. - Hands-on experience with high-speed copper interconnect products: connectors and/or cable assemblies; familiarity with patch panels or backplane/cable-backplane solutions is a plus - Strong command of problem-solving and quality tools: 8D, 5-Whys, Fishbone, PFMEA/control plans, SPC/MSA (gauge R&R), and change control. - Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, GD&T basics, and electrical/interface specifications; comfortable working across ME/EE/SI disciplines. - Experience driving supplier/CM improvements (audits, scorecards, CAPA) and managing nonconformance/MRB workflows. - Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to drive alignment across internal teams and external partners. - Experience with cable manufacturing and assembly processes (wire treatment, resistance welding/laser welding, crimping, overmolding/injection molding, braiding/shielding, plating, and automated test). - Experience with optical interconnects (AOC/DAC, pluggable modules such as QSFP/OSFP), fiber termination quality, optical return loss, end-face inspection standards (IEC 61300), and contamination control practices. - Ability to travel internationally and work effectively across time zones with ODM/JDM and supplier partners. About the Team

OpenAI is helping build the infrastructure that powers the next generation of artificial intelligence. Through Stargate, we are developing and operating large-scale AI compute campuses that require world-class execution across data center design, construction, commissioning, and operations.

The Infrastructure Operations team is responsible for bringing AI infrastructure online and ensuring it operates reliably at scale. We partner closely with hardware, network, deployment, construction, and operations teams to deliver mission-critical environments capable of supporting frontier AI workloads. As our footprint expands, operational excellence becomes increasingly important to ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient campus operations.

About the Role

We are seeking a Critical Facilities Manager to support the commissioning, operational readiness, and long-term operation of next-generation AI data center campuses.

This role sits at the intersection of construction, commissioning, hardware deployment, and facilities operations. You will be responsible for ensuring mission-critical infrastructure is prepared to support hardware deployment, transitioned successfully into production operations, and maintained to the highest standards of reliability and availability.

You will lead day-to-day operational execution across electrical, mechanical, controls, and supporting infrastructure systems while partnering closely with commissioning teams, site operators, vendors, and engineering organizations. This role requires a strong blend of technical depth, operational leadership, and cross-functional execution.

  • Lead day-to-day operations of mission-critical facility infrastructure across AI compute campuses.

  • Partner with commissioning teams to transition facilities from construction and startup into steady-state operations.

  • Manage vendors, contractors, and service providers supporting facility operations.

  • Partner with hardware deployment, networking, and engineering teams to coordinate infrastructure changes and maintenance activities.

  • Monitor facility performance, operational risk, and capacity utilization across critical systems.

  • Support staffing, training, and development of facilities operations personnel.

  • Have experience supporting commissioning, operational readiness, or infrastructure turnover programs.

  • Have led facility operations teams, contractors, and third-party vendors.

  • Are comfortable responding to incidents and making decisions in high-pressure operational environments.

  • Have experience developing maintenance strategies, operating procedures, and reliability programs.

  • Enjoy operating in fast-paced environments with significant ambiguity and rapid growth.

  • Communicate effectively across technical and non-technical stakeholders.

jobs.title: Connectivity Software Engineer, Consumer Devices
jobs.description_html:
About the Team
The Connectivity Software Engineering team is responsible for enabling seamless, secure, and high-performance wireless connectivity across OpenAI’s products. We design and optimize Bluetooth, BLE, Wi-Fi, and emerging wireless technologies to ensure robust device pairing, network performance, and interoperability. Our work spans kernel drivers, system services, and user-level tools, with a focus on real-world performance, scalability, and reliability.

About the Role
OpenAI is seeking a Connectivity Software Engineer to design, implement, and optimize wireless connectivity features across our product ecosystem. You’ll work at the intersection of systems software, wireless standards, and hardware integration—building robust pairing and provisioning flows, debugging low-level protocols, and driving performance under real-world RF constraints. You will also support certification, field interoperability, and fleet-scale connectivity infrastructure.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 4 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, implement, and debug Bluetooth/BLE and Wi-Fi features across kernel drivers, BlueZ/wpa_supplicant/hostapd, and systemd/D-Bus services

  • Deliver robust pairing, bonding, and provisioning flows (GATT/GAP, LE Audio/LC3, WPA3/802.1X, captive portals, NAN)

  • Optimize link performance: throughput, latency, jitter, roaming, coexistence (BT↔Wi-Fi), and power modes (TWT, WoWLAN)

  • Build reliable network management using NetworkManager/nmcli, nl80211/cfg80211/mac80211, DNS/DHCP/mDNS, P2P/SoftAP

  • Instrument and analyze with packet captures and tooling (btmon/hcidump, Wireshark, iperf, eBPF/perf, spectrum sniffers)

  • Drive interoperability and certification readiness (Bluetooth SIG, Wi-Fi Alliance) and resolve field issues with root-cause fixes

  • Contribute to OTA-safe configuration, telemetry, and diagnostics for fleet-scale operation

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have deep experience shipping wireless features on Linux-based products

  • Are highly proficient in C/C++ with scripting experience (Python or shell) and systems debugging (gdb, strace, logs, packet traces)

  • Possess deep knowledge of Bluetooth Classic/BLE (HCI, L2CAP, GATT/GAP, profiles) and Wi-Fi (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax, WPA2/3, nl80211, NAN)

  • Bring hands-on experience with BlueZ, wpa_supplicant/hostapd, NetworkManager, and driver bring-up on ARM64 or x86 platforms

  • Have a proven track record of improving real-world performance and reliability under RF constraints

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with LE Audio (LC3), BLE Mesh, advanced roaming (802.11k/v/r), QoS/WMM, multicast/IGMP

  • Coexistence tuning across radios (BT/Wi-Fi/UWB/mmWave) and antenna/RF fundamentals with test equipment workflows

  • Familiarity with UWB (IEEE 802.15.4z, FiRa) ranging/integration; mmWave/Wi-Gig (802.11ad/ay)

  • Experience with security and provisioning at scale (EAP-TLS, device identity, secure boot, disk/network hardening)

  • Background in building factory test, interoperability, and certification test plans; upstream/open-source contributions

jobs.title: Consumer Device Safety & Risk Operations Specialist, User Safety & Risk Operations
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

At OpenAI, our User Safety & Risk Operations (USRO) team helps protect our products and users from abuse, fraud, safety risks, and other forms of misuse. We operate at the front line of real-world safety and risk management, translating user and operational signals into timely decisions, effective interventions, and improvements to our systems.

This role sits on a team focused on building operational capacity for new, ambiguous, and fast-moving areas of work. The team defines what needs to be built, creates the operating model to support it, and works with partner teams to make the work scalable and durable over time.

About the Role

We are seeking a Device Safety & Risk Operations Specialist to build the safety operating model for a new category of consumer hardware. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who can turn emerging product risks and incomplete requirements into practical workflows, controls, launch plans, and durable systems.

You will define how product-safety incidents, critical escalations, regulated cases, and privacy-sensitive issues should be identified, investigated, escalated, resolved, and learned from. You will also establish operational requirements for case management, data access, decision logging, quality assurance, monitoring, and cross-functional response. You will stand up priority workflows through launch and early operations, then help transition them into durable homes across USRO and partner teams.

The right person combines deep operational judgment with strong technical and hardware product fluency. They can move from executive-level risk framing to detailed workflow design, tabletop exercises, launch readiness, frontline guidance, and post-launch improvement.

Location / work model: San Francisco, CA; hybrid, 3 days/week in-office.

Please note: This role may involve exposure to sensitive or concerning material. Strong discretion, judgment, and resilience are essential.


In This Role, You Will:

  • Build the end-to-end safety and risk operating model for new consumer hardware, from early requirements through launch and early-life operations.

  • Define incident taxonomies, severity levels, decision rights, escalation criteria, response pathways, and closure standards.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

The B2B Content team helps business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how to put it to work. We develop narrative, editorial, demo, and adoption programs that connect OpenAI’s products to concrete business value.

We partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Education, Sales, and other teams to create content that is useful on its own and supports the broader customer journey.

We value people who are eager to learn, have a bias for action, and look beyond the immediate deliverable. We build the tools, systems, and shared practices that help the whole team produce better work over time.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager, Demand Generation to turn foundational B2B messaging, flagship narratives, research, launches, events, and product workflows into the right content for different industries, lines of business, audiences, and stages of the customer journey.

You’ll create content across webinars, guides, ebooks, blogs, customer proof, and decision-enablement materials. You’ll also build the modular frameworks that allow strong source material to be adapted and reused without recreating the work from scratch.

You’ll work closely with Product Marketing, which owns product positioning and messaging, and Demand Generation, which owns audience and channel strategy. You’ll bring strong content judgment to that partnership: helping determine what should be created, how it should be structured, and how it can work across different contexts while preserving a coherent central narrative.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a hands-on marketer, writer, and editor. It does not include people management or ownership of the broader content portfolio.

This is a hybrid role and will be based in San Francisco, Monday through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are work-from-home days, with occasional in-office attendance as needed for live webinars.

In this role, you will

  • Partner with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, the Senior Narrative Writer, the Adoption Content Marketer, and Demo Studio to identify strong source material and define the content plan for priority programs.

  • Create and adapt content across webinars, flagship guides and ebooks, thought-leadership blogs, solution and buyer guides, customer proof, and decision-enablement materials.

  • Turn core assets into reusable modules for specific industries, lines of business, use cases, and executive, practitioner, and technical audiences.

  • Develop awareness-, consideration-, and decision-stage versions of priority content while preserving the central narrative.

  • Find the strongest narrative, proof point, or value proposition within complex source material and translate it into clear, useful content.

  • Collaborate with Demand Generation and channel partners to ensure content is designed for real audience and distribution needs.

  • Use audience and performance signals to improve how future content is structured, packaged, and reused.

  • Establish repeatable frameworks, templates, and practices that increase the return on major content investments.

  • Maintain strong editorial quality across a high volume of interconnected assets.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have 7+ years of experience in B2B content marketing, editorial, integrated campaigns, or a related discipline.

  • Are an exceptional writer and editor with a portfolio showing how you adapted substantive source material for different B2B audiences and contexts.

  • Can translate complex B2B product and business subject matter into content that is clear without becoming simplistic.

  • Know how to identify the strongest B2B narrative, proof point, or value proposition within a larger body of material.

  • Have experience creating B2B content across industries, business functions, buyer groups, or stages of the customer journey.

  • Understand B2B audience and channel needs and can collaborate closely with Demand Generation without losing the integrity of the central narrative.

  • Can create both high-quality individual assets and the systems that make future work faster and more consistent.

  • Combine strong editorial judgment with speed, precision, and comfort working across a high volume of interconnected work.

jobs.title: Content Studio Lead
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

This team is for people who are energized by ambiguity, intellectually curious, and excited to build something enduring from the beginning.

About the Role

As Content Studio Creative Lead, you will build and lead a centralized content studio that serves the broader creative team. You will be both a senior maker and a capability builder: creating timely, high-quality content while shaping the studio’s creative approach, talent network, and quality standards, in partnership with Production on the processes that support the work at scale.

We’re looking for someone who can move fluidly between hands-on content creation and creative systems thinking. You will work closely with leaders, researchers, creative teams, and external partners to capture stories at the source and turn them into compelling work for web, social, and the broader OpenAI brand.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. Travel for production may be required.

In this role, you will:

  • Define the content studio’s creative vision, creative strategy, and measures of quality and effectiveness, and partner with Production on production workflows.

  • Identify the right creative talent and partners across internal teams, freelancers, and agencies, working with Production to build the team and production approach around each project.

  • Create reusable formats, playbooks, and standards that help teams produce strong work quickly across web, social, editorial, and brand channels.

  • Partner with creative leads to prioritize requests and set the creative ambition and craft needs for each opportunity. Work with Production to make shared decisions on scope, budget, tradeoffs, and how to bring the work to life.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of building or significantly scaling a content, production, editorial, or studio capability.

  • Are an accomplished content maker with strong editorial judgment and a portfolio spanning multiple formats and channels.

  • Can personally develop and create high-priority content with leaders, researchers, customers, and external partners, from concept through delivery.

  • Can creatively lead work from concept through delivery while partnering with Production and remaining hands-on when the work demands it.

  • Build trust quickly with senior leaders, technical experts, creative collaborators, and external talent.

  • Bring operational rigor, resourcefulness, and calm decision-making to fast-moving production environments.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Sourcing and Procurement organization helps the company acquire and scale the products, services, and partnerships needed to advance its mission. As the organization grows, we are looking for a strategic builder-operator to establish an AI-led contracting capability that improves speed, consistency, and execution across the company.

As a Contract Management Lead, you will build, lead, and continuously improve OpenAI’s AI-led contracting help desk—a new capability designed to scale contract drafting, review, negotiation, and lifecycle management without significantly increasing headcount. You will own the service strategy, operating model, delivery oversight, coordinator enablement, workflow design, and performance tracking. Sourcing coordinators will manage day-to-day negotiations and agreement execution; you will ensure they have the tools, playbooks, training, guidance, and escalation support required to deliver timely, consistent, and well-governed outcomes.

You will use a contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform as the central system of record, connect it with procurement tools and contract repositories, and partner with Legal, Procurement, Engineering, sourcing coordinators, and CLM technology partners to pilot, evaluate, and improve emerging AI capabilities. Your work will turn contracting into a trusted, measurable, continuously improving service.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the product vision and roadmap for an AI-led contracting help desk, translating user needs into a scalable, measurable service for contract intake, triage, and lifecycle management.

  • Build and continuously improve the AI-enabled contracting framework, including agent-assisted drafting, clause and fallback recommendations, negotiation guidance, risk detection, and human-in-the-loop escalation.

  • Own the contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform and system of record, including workflows, approved templates and playbooks, metadata, reporting, and integrations with procurement tools and repositories.

  • Enable sourcing coordinators to lead day-to-day negotiations and agreement execution through effective training, clear ownership, service levels, and operational support.

  • Partner with Legal, Procurement, Engineering, Security, Privacy, and Finance to define approval guardrails, resolve escalations, and deploy AI responsibly.

  • Pilot emerging contract lifecycle management and AI capabilities; measure cycle time, automation, quality, coordinator delivery, and stakeholder adoption; and use those insights to improve the service.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Bring an AI-forward mindset, with experience building or deploying AI-enabled agents, automation, or decision-support workflows and a practical understanding of evaluation, human review, confidentiality, and operational safeguards.

  • Think and operate like a product manager: identify user needs, define a roadmap, prioritize workflows, launch pilots, and continuously improve the experience using data and feedback.

  • Bring strong commercial contracting and legal-language judgment; a JD, law degree, or comparable legal background is strongly preferred, but exceptional equivalent experience is welcome.

  • Have implemented or owned a contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform and can design templates, clause libraries, integrations, reporting, and scalable workflows.

  • Can build and run a service model that enables sourcing coordinators, clarifies ownership, tracks delivery, and escalates risk without personally owning every negotiation.

  • Build trusted cross-functional partnerships and bring structure, speed, and sound judgment to ambiguous, high-stakes operational problems.

jobs.title: Control Systems Software Engineer, Robotics
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role
We’re looking for a Robotics Control Systems Engineer to take on a foundational role within our robotics team. You’ll help architect, implement, tune, and verify the control infrastructure that enables intelligent, reliable, and responsive robot behavior.

This is a deeply hands-on role focused on real-time systems, actuation, dynamics, low-level hardware interaction, and whole-robot performance. You’ll spend significant time working directly with robots onsite: debugging behavior, tuning subsystems, running experiments, and providing feedback across mechanical, electrical, and software teams.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person 5 days a week.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement real-time control algorithms for robotic systems, including motion control, feedback loops, state estimation, actuator control, and subsystem tuning.

  • Define the control architecture from low-level actuators and hardware interfaces through whole-robot behavior and policy.

  • Identify and characterize actuator, hardware, and software parameters through rigorous experimentation, testing, commissioning, and verification.

  • Work with machine learning engineers to implement reinforcement learning models.

  • Collaborate across mechanical, electrical, and software teams to integrate control logic with sensing and actuation hardware.

  • Help inform the mechanical and electrical design to maximize capability and flexibility.

  • Create the control system architecture; determine the correct level of abstraction from actuators all the way up to whole-robot policy.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong robotics background, including manipulators, mobile robots, or other complex physical systems.

  • Have experience with actuation, control systems, robot dynamics, estimation, subsystem tuning, or whole-body motion.

  • Are comfortable being hands-on with robotic hardware, including commissioning, debugging, testing, and iterating on real robots.

  • Have strong fundamentals in classical control, system dynamics, and estimation, with exposure to modern learning-based or reinforcement learning approaches.

  • Can move comfortably across the stack, from low-level actuator behavior and hardware interfaces to higher-level algorithms and whole-robot performance.

  • Have experience writing performant production-quality software in C++ or Rust.

  • Experience with robotic hardware and enjoy iterating quickly between simulation and real-world testing environments.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

The Corporate Development team sits at the intersection of OpenAI’s strategy and the global AI ecosystem. Partnering closely with engineering, product, and business leaders, we analyze markets, technologies, and companies to identify opportunities that accelerate OpenAI’s mission and long-term strategy. Bringing together expertise in strategy, M&A, and integration, the team leads the end-to-end process of sourcing, evaluating, negotiating, and integrating acquisitions and other strategic transactions.

About the Role

The Corporate Development Deal Lead will own high-priority M&A and strategic transaction work from early evaluation through diligence, structuring, negotiation, approval, and close. This person will translate strategic priorities and market insight into actionable deal opportunities, build the business case for transactions, and drive cross-functional alignment with senior stakeholders.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who can combine strategic judgment, financial rigor, founder relationship-building, and crisp execution. The ideal candidate can lead complex transactions, partner well with executive stakeholders, and help build the AI-native systems, tools, and operating practices that allow Corp Dev to scale.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead end-to-end execution of corporate development transactions (e.g., acquisitions and strategic investments), including sourcing, diligence, valuation, structuring, negotiation, and closing.

  • Track and interpret key trends across AI, technology, and adjacent industries, translating the competitive and startup landscape into clear, high-impact insights for OpenAI’s leadership.

  • Proactively source acquisition and other opportunities by building deep relationships across the venture, startup, and incubator ecosystem.

  • Partner closely with internal leaders to understand OpenAI’s priorities and use external market intelligence to help shape strategy and identify where inorganic moves can accelerate it.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, GTM, and executive leadership to evaluate and advance deals.

  • Build financial models, commercial cases, and decision-making frameworks for executive stakeholders.

  • Prepare and present deal materials to senior leaders.

  • Lead and innovate how we use AI to enhance Corp Dev processes and systems.

  • Partner with Integration & cross-functional peers to develop deal goals / metrics and integration plans to achieve and measure outcomes.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 12+ years of experience leading M&A or strategic transactions from start to finish - in corporate development, private equity, investment banking, venture investing, and/or product.

  • Deep experience analyzing emerging technologies and markets, and enjoy working directly with founders, investors, and operators. Sector and deal expertise in enterprise / B2B highly preferred.

  • A genuine passion for AI and its impact on the world.

  • Strong analytical skills combined with commercial judgment and strategic insight.

  • Comfort managing ambiguity, building process in a fast-moving environment, and operating with high ownership.

  • Clear and persuasive communication skills to influence internal and external stakeholders.

  • Excitement to help build and shape the Corp Dev function at a mission-driven AI company.

jobs.title: Corporate Security Manager - Americas
jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Corporate Security (CorpSec) team protects our people, places, and operations so that employees can safely pursue our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The team partners across the company to enable a secure, resilient, and trusted environment that supports both safety and innovation.

We operate in dynamic, high-visibility environments, including dense urban offices and major events where discretion, credibility, and sound judgment are essential. The Corporate Security team works closely with Real Estate & Workplace, Legal, Communications, HR, IT, and external partners to maintain a proactive and people-first security posture.

About the Role

The Security Operations Manager owns day-to-day physical security operations and end-to-end security programs across assigned sites. The role is accountable for vendor performance, staffing and training plans, incident readiness, and recurring operational improvements that protect OpenAI’s people, facilities, and business activities.

The ideal candidate combines hands-on operational leadership with independent program ownership, sound judgment, and strong cross-functional partnerships. They anticipate risks, resolve competing operational priorities, build repeatable procedures, and coordinate effective incident responses while escalating material risks and resource decisions through established channels.

This role reports to the Senior Security Operations Manager and will include both domestic and international travel in support of Event Security, and other CorpSec ongoing and developing initiatives.

In this role you will:

  • Office Security: Security Operations & Program Ownership: Own security operating plans and program outcomes across assigned sites, including guard coverage, staffing and training plans, access control, visitor management, post orders, and emergency readiness. Set clear expectations for contracted providers and review staffing, schedules, service quality, invoices, and corrective actions within delegated budget and contract authority. This is a great opportunity to join OpenAI’s commercial legal team, negotiating high-impact agreements and helping to build scalable frameworks for responsible growth.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI's Business Marketing team helps companies understand and adopt our products and platform. The team develops integrated programs for business leaders, technical decision-makers, developers, and enterprise customers across launches, campaigns, brand, content, web and digital experiences, events, customer storytelling, and sales enablement.

We work across Marketing, Creative, Product, Sales, Communications, and external partners to turn complex technology into useful, credible stories and experiences.

About the Role

As the Delivery Lead for Business Marketing, you will own end-to-end production and delivery across the B2B marketing portfolio. This role combines the scope of an executive producer with portfolio delivery and people leadership across creative and digital work. You will be accountable for everything that must ship: turning priorities and briefs into executable plans, assigning the right teams, managing dependencies and decisions, and carrying work through launch and final handoff.

You will lead producers and project managers while staying hands-on with the most complex or high-priority work. You will create a clear view of the portfolio, make practical tradeoffs, remove obstacles, and serve as the primary delivery escalation point for internal teams and agency partners.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will

  • Own end-to-end delivery across the full B2B marketing portfolio, including integrated campaigns, launches, brand and content programs, web and digital experiences, events, customer stories, and sales enablement.

  • Lead, coach, and allocate work across producers and project managers, with clear ownership, operating standards, and escalation paths.

  • Personally produce the highest-priority or most complex initiatives and stay close enough to the work to resolve difficult delivery problems.

  • Turn business goals and creative briefs into executable plans with clear scope, deliverables, milestones, resources, budgets, dependencies, approvers, and definitions of done.

  • Maintain an integrated view of active and upcoming work so teams can see priorities, capacity, timelines, dependencies, risks, and decisions in one place.

  • Coordinate reviews, decisions, and handoffs across marketing, creative, digital, product, sales, communications, agencies, and other contributors.

  • Own agency and production-partner delivery, including scoping, kickoff, working rhythms, budgets, risk management, and performance.

  • Identify delivery risks early, remove obstacles, make tradeoffs, and escalate the decisions that require senior leadership judgment.

  • Ensure approvals, usage rights, final assets, source files, and delivery documentation are complete and easy to find.

  • Build practical production and project-management methods that improve planning, quality, and throughput as the B2B portfolio and team grow.

  • Provide concise delivery reporting on what has shipped, what is next, what is at risk, and where decisions are needed; lead retrospectives and put agreed improvements into practice.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have 10+ years leading a complex, high-volume portfolio of integrated marketing and creative work across both traditional and digital channels.

  • Bring deep creative-production expertise and a strong command of digital delivery workflows, including web and content experiences.

  • Have managed and developed both producers and project managers, and know how to build a team as the work scales.

  • Can turn incomplete briefs, changing priorities, and compressed timelines into clear plans without losing momentum or quality.

  • Use strong portfolio judgment to sequence work, balance capacity, and make tradeoffs across competing priorities.

  • Are experienced in managing agencies, production partners, scopes, budgets, and vendor performance.

  • Communicate clearly with senior stakeholders and working teams, and create the conditions for fast, well-informed decisions.

  • Balance a detailed command of delivery with a systems-level view of how the full portfolio fits together.

  • Operate as a leader-doer: collaborative, steady under pressure, willing to work through hard details, and biased toward action.

jobs.title: Creative Director, Art
jobs.description_html:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood, as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told, in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Creative Director, Art to join our in-house creative team, focused on OpenAI’s business audiences. In this role, you’ll shape the visual direction and creative expression of our B2B brand across integrated campaigns, product launches, customer storytelling, and key industry moments.

You’ll help translate the capabilities of OpenAI’s technology into clear and compelling stories for business leaders, technical decision-makers, developers, and teams bringing AI into their organizations. The strongest work will make sophisticated products understandable without oversimplifying them—and connect what the technology can do with the real needs, ambitions, and outcomes of our customers.

This role sits at the intersection of conceptual thinking, visual craft, and business storytelling. You’ll partner closely with writers, designers, product marketers, sales and customer teams, product leaders, and external collaborators to develop big ideas and bring them to life across formats—from integrated campaigns and digital experiences to customer stories, films, events, and product storytelling.

  • Build visual systems that can extend across the B2B customer journey, from awareness and product education to industry events and customer engagement

  • Help evolve OpenAI’s visual language for business audiences in ways that are distinctive, scalable, and expressive while remaining connected to the broader brand

  • Lead multiple creative initiatives simultaneously with clarity, strong judgment, and creative conviction

  • Have experience creating work for B2B, enterprise, developer, or other technically sophisticated audiences

  • Are a conceptual thinker who can develop big creative ideas and guide them from early strategy through execution

  • Know how to turn complex products, technical capabilities, and business challenges into visual stories that are clear, human, and memorable

  • Have experience leading integrated campaigns and large-scale brand initiatives across different stages of the customer journey

  • Can balance the need for enterprise credibility with the desire to create distinctive, culturally relevant work

  • Are comfortable operating in fast-moving environments with evolving priorities, multiple stakeholders, and complex creative challenges

  • Have exceptional design taste and a deep commitment to visual craft and storytelling

  • Are a strong cross-functional collaborator who works effectively with creative, product marketing, product, sales, communications, and production partners

  • Have experience guiding work through internal teams, agencies, and external creative vendors

  • Balance creative ambition with clarity, precision, and strategic thinking

  • Experience working on enterprise technology, developer platforms, AI, or emerging products

  • Experience creating campaigns for audiences that span executive buyers, technical decision-makers, developers, and end users

  • Motion design or film art direction experience

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored.
