jobs.title: Wireless Regulatory Engineer - SAR
jobs.description_html:
Wireless Regulatory Engineer – SAR

About the Team

The Consumer Devices team at OpenAI builds products that bring advanced AI capabilities into thoughtfully designed consumer experiences. We work across hardware, software, design, and research to develop reliable products from early exploration through production.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Wireless Regulatory Engineer to support RF exposure compliance for consumer hardware. You’ll work closely with RF, antenna, hardware, software, and regulatory teams throughout the product development lifecycle, helping ensure products meet applicable requirements while maintaining a high bar for performance and user experience.

This role is based in Mountain View, CA. We use a hybrid work model of four days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop and execute RF exposure test and validation strategies for consumer wireless products.

  • Partner with engineering teams to evaluate product designs and identify potential compliance risks throughout development.

  • Perform and analyze RF exposure measurements and communicate findings clearly to cross-functional teams.

  • Support product development from early prototypes through validation, certification, and production.

  • Coordinate testing with external laboratories and review results and supporting documentation.

  • Translate applicable regulatory requirements into practical engineering guidance.

  • Partner with RF and antenna teams to balance regulatory requirements with product performance.

  • Develop tools and workflows that improve testing efficiency, consistency, and data analysis.

  • Investigate issues, identify root causes, and work with engineering teams to develop effective solutions.

  • Support global regulatory certification activities for wireless consumer products.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, RF Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Bring deep experience with SAR, RF exposure, or wireless regulatory testing.

  • Have a strong understanding of RF fundamentals, measurement techniques, and wireless systems.

  • Have experience translating regulatory requirements into engineering and product decisions.

  • Are comfortable performing hands-on testing, analyzing complex measurement data, and troubleshooting hardware systems.

  • Have experience working with external test laboratories and supporting product certification.

  • Collaborate effectively across RF, antenna, hardware, software, manufacturing, and operations teams.

  • Are comfortable working in fast-moving, ambiguous product development environments.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in SAR, RF exposure, wireless regulatory engineering, or a closely related field.

  • Experience supporting consumer hardware from prototype through mass production.

  • Experience with wireless products incorporating multiple radios and connectivity technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing test automation or data-analysis tools.

  • Experience supporting regulatory approvals across multiple global markets.

  • Experience working on products that integrate hardware, firmware, and software.

jobs.description_html:
About the Team

OpenAI's People team helps hire, develop, and support the people building safe and beneficial AGI. Within that team, People Systems builds the technical foundation that enables our HR, recruiting, payroll, benefits, and performance operations to scale with quality, speed, and rigor.

We work at the intersection of HR systems, software engineering, and internal tooling. Our goal is not just to keep core systems running, but to build durable technical leverage for the company.

About the Role

We're hiring a Workday Engineer to help design, build, and operate the systems that power critical people workflows at OpenAI.

This is a highly technical role for someone who combines strong Workday expertise with real engineering fluency. You'll build reliable integrations, improve system architecture, automate complex workflows, and help connect Workday to internal tools, external platforms, and emerging AI-driven systems.

You should be comfortable going beyond configuration work. We're looking for someone who can reason through ambiguous systems problems, write and debug technical solutions, work effectively in Git-based environments, and use modern developer workflows, including CLI-driven tooling, to build and operate with speed and discipline.

You'll partner closely with cross-functional teams across People, Finance, Security, and Engineering, including our People Innovations team, to build systems that are secure, scalable, and practical. Some work will involve improving mature production infrastructure; some will involve building entirely new workflows and capabilities from scratch.

In this role, you will

  • Design, build, and maintain Workday integrations, applications, and workflow automations across domains such as payroll, benefits, recruiting, performance, and case management

  • Improve the reliability, quality, and scalability of People systems through strong engineering, testing, and operational practices

  • Build technical solutions that connect Workday with internal platforms, external vendors, and AI-powered tooling

  • Contribute to more agentic internal workflows by helping design systems that combine HR data, automation, orchestration, and intelligent tooling

  • Use Git-based development practices, code review, and structured change management to deliver safely in a fast-moving environment

  • Use CLI-based tools and developer workflows to build, test, troubleshoot, and support production systems efficiently

  • Partner with stakeholders across People, Finance, Security, and Engineering to translate business needs into durable technical solutions

  • Establish and raise standards for observability, security, supportability, and long-term maintainability across the People systems stack

You might thrive in this role if you have

  • 5-10 years of experience in Workday engineering, integrations, platform automation, or adjacent systems engineering roles

  • Strong hands-on experience with Workday technologies such as EIB, Studio, Cloud Connect, Extend, reporting, calculated fields, security, and business process design

  • A track record of building technical solutions beyond administration or configuration alone, including automation, scripting, debugging, and systems design

  • Comfort working in Git-based environments with modern software development practices

  • Strong fluency with CLI-based workflows and developer tools

  • Experience designing and supporting production integrations with a high bar for reliability, security, and data quality

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through ambiguous technical and operational challenges

  • The ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical partners

  • Interest in agentic systems, AI-enabled internal tooling, or LLM-powered workflow design

Nice to have

  • Experience integrating Workday with finance systems, identity systems, recruiting tools, case management platforms, or internal developer platforms

  • Experience with observability, alerting, and production support for business-critical workflows

  • Experience building internal tools or automation frameworks in high-growth environments

  • Familiarity with secure systems design and governance in environments handling sensitive employee data

jobs.title: Workforce Development & Education Manager, Infrastructure Sites
jobs.description_html:
About the Role

At OpenAI, we are proud to build and operate our data centers with a community-first led approach. From construction to operations, we want to be positive partners within our data center communities that we are honored to call home…and we are just getting started.

OpenAI is seeking a Workforce Development & Education Manager to help build local talent for data center construction, commissioning, and operations in communities hosting OpenAI infrastructure projects. You will work with infrastructure teams and project partners, education providers, and local Community Engagement Leads to understand workforce needs and help education and training providers prepare people for these jobs of the future.

You will build partnerships with local community colleges, technical schools, universities, and union apprenticeship programs from the ground up. Working with educators and technical experts, you will develop and expand training programs that connect local residents with career opportunities and meet the local industry hiring needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Work in partnership with the local Community Engagement Lead to build and manage relationships with community colleges, technical schools, universities, career and technical education programs, and local workforce boards.

  • Work with building trades unions and joint apprenticeship and training committees to expand training opportunities aligned with project needs both on a local and national level.

  • Partner with OpenAI’s infrastructure teams, developers, contractors, and operators to identify job requirements, skills gaps, and hiring timelines across construction, commissioning, and operations.

  • Work with educators and technical experts to develop or adapt curricula, hands-on training, and credential programs that reflect employer requirements and offerings available through OpenAI’s literacy programs.

  • Support apprenticeships, internships, and other work-based learning opportunities with participating employers.

  • Manage program implementation, including timelines, partner responsibilities, and progress against agreed goals.

  • Track participation, completion, credential attainment, job placement, and retention, working with partners to use the results to improve programs.

  • Partner with the local Community Engagement Lead to identify workforce grants and other funding opportunities, and help education and training partners pursue relevant support.

  • Represent OpenAI on local workforce advisory councils and in meetings with education, labor, and community partners, in partnership with the Community Engagement Lead.

  • Manage the program operations and administrative tasks needed to run a successful workforce development program within our data center communities.

Qualifications

  • Seven or more years of experience in workforce development, technical education, apprenticeship programs, or education–industry partnerships.

  • Bachelor’s degree in education, instructional design, workforce development, engineering technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Experience developing and delivering technical training programs with employers and education providers.

  • Experience working with trade unions, apprenticeship programs, and labor leaders.

  • Ability to work with technical experts to translate job requirements into clear learning objectives and practical training.

  • Experience managing programs with multiple partners, competing priorities, and defined deadlines.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience working with educators, public officials, labor representatives, and technical leaders.

  • Experience evaluating program outcomes and using findings to improve delivery.

  • Experience in operating with ambiguity and building successful programs from the ground up, with responsible scalability in mind.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in data centers, telecommunications, semiconductor manufacturing, energy, or other industries with substantial technical workforce needs.

  • Familiarity with training and credentials relevant to data center careers, such as OSHA 30-hour and NFPA 70E safety training, Schneider Electric DCCA, BICSI cabling credentials, CompTIA certifications, and EPA Section 608 certification for refrigerant work.

  • Experience with workforce funding sources, including Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act programs, apprenticeship grants, and state workforce or community college grants.

  • Experience helping local residents enter skilled trades and technical careers through community-based education and training partnerships.

About the Team

OpenAI’s Applications Engineering organization builds and operates the products that bring our cutting-edge research to millions of users and developers worldwide. The Applied Foundations team owns the core product and platform layers that make those experiences possible — from identity & access, to safety to payments & commerce across all of our apps. Our teams span product engineering, infrastructure, and safety, working together to deliver technology that is reliable, secure, and trusted at global scale.

About the Role

You will be a Senior iOS engineer on OpenAI’s Applied Foundations team, building the core mobile experiences that power how users sign up, manage their account, family features, pay for services, stay safe, and interact with OpenAI’s products with confidence. This role is about creating high-quality products as well as reusable iOS foundations that product teams across different OpenAI apps depend on to ship quickly while meeting the highest standards for security, reliability, and user trust. You’ll own complex client-side systems spanning UI, networking, local state, payment integrations and Apple platform integrations, and work closely with backend, product, and safety partners to shape the architecture that supports OpenAI’s mobile ecosystem at global scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and ship new experiences on iOS that showcase the power of AI.

  • Optimize app performance, reliability, and responsiveness at global scale.

  • Design and maintain shared iOS frameworks and primitives for account, trust, and commerce flows that are used across OpenAI’s mobile apps.

  • Establish robust testing frameworks and refine app architecture for long-term maintainability.

  • Collaborate with product, design, research, and backend teams to deliver high-impact features.

  • Provide technical leadership to shape the future of OpenAI’s iOS platform.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 4+ years of professional software engineering experience.

  • Have a proven track record of building high-quality iOS applications in production, especially for systems that need to be reliable and resilient at scale.

  • Have owned complex, business-critical mobile systems end-to-end.

  • Have experience making deep architectural tradeoffs on iOS.

  • Are fluent in Swift and familiar with the Apple development ecosystem (Xcode, UIKit, SwiftUI).

  • Care deeply about performance, security, and user experience.

  • Enjoy working cross-functionally to bring ambitious product ideas to life.

jobs.title: AI Engagement Manager
jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across the US and London— we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, Seattle, and London

We are looking for a highly-motivated senior IC who will work with some of Runway’s biggest and most strategic partners. You will be central to our partners’ success in adopting Runway to transform the ways they create content. Success in this role will require a mix of technical fluency, strategic thinking, and hands-on execution.

What you’ll do

  • Own deep, trusted C-suite level relationships with Runway's most strategic partners (from Hollywood studios to Fortune 100 enterprises) ensuring they're not just customers, but long-term partners at the frontier of AI-driven creativity and innovation

  • Be in the room where it happens: collaborating directly with world-class creative teams at the biggest Hollywood studios, brands, and F100 companies to co-create Emmy award-winning shows, Oscar-winning movies, Super Bowl commercials, and cultural moments that define a generation

  • Operate as a strategic thought partner internally: codifying the use cases we know work today while pioneering the ones that don't exist yet, and translating both into initiatives that shape Runway's product strategy and industry positioning

  • Get embedded within accounts to learn and understand their (content) pain points and challenges today, then propose discrete ways in which Runway can solve those challenges

  • Identify and prototype specific and highly targeted new markets and new opportunities for our products

  • Develop a deep, functional and technical understanding of our products and future roadmap

  • Be hands-on in quickly onboarding new partners to our platform and/or API while also supporting their long-term expansion and technical understanding of how to leverage Runway

  • Provide high-impact feedback to Product, Engineering, and Creative which can in turn improve the product experience for our partners

  • Analyze, track, and report on the performance of existing partnerships leveraging BI tools and data

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years of overall experience in customer-facing roles, engaging C-level technical audiences with complex global organizations ideally within tech, finance, or consulting

  • Have led complex implementations of Generative AI/traditional ML solutions and can drive measurable business outcomes

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities with expansive ownership and ruthlessly prioritize

  • A strong bias towards action and belief that no task is too small for you

  • Have a track record of rapidly prototyping ideas and a willingness to work iteratively with your customers to deliver the right solution that solves their problem

  • Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when engaging with executives and leaders

  • High technical aptitude for understanding complex technologies, tools, systems, and issues

  • Mindset to think creatively and think beyond past checklists and playbooks

  • Highly resourceful with the ability to create structure and work autonomously amidst ambiguity

  • Nice to have but not required: experience with data tooling and BI systems (SQL, BigQuery, Retool, etc)

  • New York, SF, or London-based preferred

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

Working at Runway

Great things come from great teams. We’d love to hear from you.

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. So regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply.

More about Runway

  • Universal World Simulator

  • GWM-1

  • Gen-4.5

  • General World Models

  • Robotics SDK

  • Conversational Real-time Agents

  • Runway Studios

We're excited to be recognized as a best place to work:

Crain's | InHerSight | BuiltIn NYC | INC

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, and Seattle

We’re looking for a Business Development Representative to continue building the outbound motion at Runway and support our GTM Sales team across Enterprise and Mid Market.

In this role, you will partner closely with our Enterprise and Mid Market account executives to identify, research, and engage high-potential accounts. You’ll help refine our outbound strategy, messaging, and targeting while creating pipeline with some of the most innovative brands, studios, and technology companies in the world.

As we continue to scale the team, this role offers meaningful ownership and the opportunity to influence how prospecting and account development are done at Runway. Over time, there may also be opportunities to run and close smaller SMB deals, giving you exposure to the full sales cycle.

This role is ideal for someone who is curious, resourceful, and excited about building and refining processes in a fast-moving environment.

What you’ll do

  • Partner closely with our GTM Sales team to research and prioritize target accounts

  • Identify and engage stakeholders across creative, marketing, production, and technology teams

  • Develop thoughtful outbound campaigns across email, phone, and other channels

  • Craft compelling, highly personalized messaging tailored to brand-driven and technical organizations

  • Generate qualified pipeline and schedule meetings for our Enterprise and Mid Market account executives

  • Experiment with messaging, targeting, and sequencing to improve engagement and conversion

  • Maintain clear notes and activity in CRM tools to support coordinated account strategy

  • Share feedback from prospects to help inform positioning, product direction, and go-to-market strategy

  • Over time, manage and close select SMB or smaller expansion opportunities, gaining exposure to discovery, qualification, and closing

As part of a growing team, you’ll have the chance to help define best practices, contribute to playbooks, and influence how the BDR function evolves at Runway.

What you’ll need

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex ideas clearly and concisely

  • Lead negotiations with Runway’s customers and strategic partners. These include B2B SaaS customer contracts for our generative AI SaaS platform and APIs, DPAs, partnership agreements, and vendor agreements.

  • Empower the sales team with tools and knowledge to close deals quickly

  • Dive into the technical aspects of our generative AI products to learn them inside and out, to inform your advice to the business

  • Closely follow technical, legal, and policy developments in the generative AI space

What you’ll need

  • A J.D. and admission in good standing with at least one state bar

  • 3+ years of negotiating complex technology transactions, including 1+ years negotiating B2B SAAS customer contracts on a commercial legal team at a fast-paced late stage private or mid-sized public B2B SaaS company

  • In addition to B2B SaaS customer contract negotiations, experience with data privacy, legal operations, strategic IP-heavy partnerships and preferably B2C legal issues are nice-to-have

  • Bias for action and a willingness to take ownership

  • Growth mindset that prioritizes continuous operational improvement and service excellence

  • Experience with scaling business processes globally and operating in environments that have achieved significant scale

  • Excitement about generative AI and motivation to continuously learn more about the legal landscape governing a new and exciting industry

About the role

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

We're looking for a Copywriter with a focus in Product Marketing to sit at the intersection of product marketing and in-product experience. This is not a brand or campaign role — it's a performance-driven, product-close writing role. You'll own copy across landing pages, lifecycle emails, ads, feature launches, onboarding flows, in-product messaging, and everything in between. You'll report to the Creative Director of Product Marketing.

Your work will directly shape how people discover, understand, and adopt Runway's products. That means writing copy that converts on a landing page, writing the in-product text that helps a user get started, and crafting the email that brings them back. You'll partner closely with product marketing, growth, design, and product teams — and you'll be measured on clarity, speed, and impact.

What you'll do

  • Write landing page copy, ad copy, and performance marketing assets that drive acquisition and conversion

  • Own in-product copy — onboarding flows, feature announcements, tooltips, modals, upgrade prompts, and CTAs

  • Write lifecycle and product emails — launches, re-engagement, onboarding sequences, and feature adoption

  • Own the narrative for launch videos and short-form product films, writing scripts, sharpening others' drafts, and making sure every frame makes the product's value clear

  • Partner with product marketing on positioning, messaging frameworks, and go-to-market copy for new releases

  • Collaborate with design and product teams to shape the in-product writing experience

  • Write and iterate on A/B test variants across landing pages, emails, and ads

  • Translate complex, technical product capabilities into clear, compelling language for a range of audiences

  • Maintain consistency in product voice and terminology across all touchpoints

What you'll need

  • 4+ years of experience in product copywriting, growth marketing or a related writing role at a tech or SaaS company

  • A portfolio that shows range across performance marketing, product copy and in-product writing — not just brand campaigns

  • Strong instinct for conversion-oriented writing — you think in terms of clarity, action, and outcomes

  • Experience writing in-product copy (onboarding, feature education, UX microcopy) alongside marketing copy

  • Comfort working with data — you can look at test results, funnel metrics and engagement data and know what to write next

  • Experience partnering with product, design, and growth teams in a fast-moving environment

  • Ability to context-switch across multiple launches and workstreams without losing quality

  • Experience in AI, creative tools, or developer-adjacent products is a strong plus

*Open to hiring remote across the US — we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, and Seattle

Runway is growing fast, and so is the surface area of what users need to learn. We're looking for an Education Content Specialist to keep our Help Center accurate, our Academy content well-produced, and our users set up for success from day one.

You'll sit within the Experience & Enterprise Enablement team, working closely with the Education & Enablement lead to execute against a content roadmap that spans written documentation, video scripts, and self-service resources. Every feature launch will have your fingerprints on it. You're the person who makes sure users don't have to guess.

What you’ll do

  • Write, update, and maintain Help Center articles across product features, billing, policies, and troubleshooting — keeping documentation accurate as the product moves fast

  • Coordinate with engineering and product at launch time to ensure articles are live before features ship

  • Audit existing Help Center content for accuracy and discoverability; surface recommendations based on support ticket trends and user feedback

  • Create and maintain self-service content — FAQs, quick-start guides, troubleshooting flows — that reduces ticket volume and helps users help themselves

  • Draft scripts for Runway Academy video tutorials, walkthroughs, and course modules

  • Support production of Academy content: create supporting assets, prepare materials for recording, and help get finished content published and organized

  • Build and maintain a library of templates, prompt guides, and project starters across Runway's tools

  • Support production and publishing of office hours, webinars, and live Q&A sessions

  • Keep Help Center documentation and Academy content consistent and cross-referenced

  • Track the performance of content you've produced — article engagement, search deflection, CSAT — and flag gaps to the Education & Enablement lead

  • Work with legal to ensure usage policies and terms are accurately reflected in customer-facing content

What you’ll need

  • 2-3 years of experience in technical writing, documentation, education content, or a similar role at a software or SaaS company

  • Ability to translate complex product features into clear, user-friendly language — across articles, scripts, and guides

  • Experience shipping documentation on tight timelines with cross-functional dependencies

  • Comfort with help center platforms (Zendesk, Intercom, or similar) and content management systems

  • Familiarity with video content production and an instinct for how to structure and pace educational content

  • Strong editorial judgment — you catch inconsistencies before they go live

  • Organized and autonomous working style; you can manage a documentation backlog while staying responsive to urgent launch needs

  • A bias toward action and a belief that no task is too small

  • Familiarity building with LLMs to streamline and automate processes

Nice to have

  • Experience with AI or creative tools — with genuine curiosity about how they work

  • Background in or passion for the creative space — video, design, animation, or related fields

  • Experience using support data (ticket volume, search queries, CSAT, completion rates) to prioritize content work

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

About the role

We are looking for a passionate Design Engineer to join Runway Labs — our research and exploration team pushing the frontier of AI video and General World Models. This is not a role focused on Runway core consumer products; instead, you’ll be embedded in a fast-moving lab environment where the work is exploratory, experimental, and technical.

This candidate should be a motivated self-starter with experience working closely with engineering and research teams to rapidly prototype and ship. You'll explore new interfaces and interaction paradigms for AI generated video, world models, and agentic systems helping translate cutting-edge research into tangible, usable experiences.

This role requires a blend of design skills and technical expertise, along with a genuine passion for both. As part of a small team, you’ll collaborate with researchers, engineers, and product designers to develop concept prototypes, design high-value interactive features, and build tools that enable new creative and research workflows.

What you’ll do

  • Prototype and implement novel user experiences at the intersection of AI video, world models, and emerging generative media

  • Design and build agentic tools and interfaces that allow researchers and creatives to interact with and direct AI systems in real time

  • Explore new application areas for AI video and general world models — from simulation and interactive media to research tooling

  • Stretch the limits of front-end engineering to broaden what’s possible in research and experimentation contexts

  • Create internal tools and frameworks used across design and engineering teams at Runway Labs

  • Work alongside researchers, engineers, and product designers to shape how we think about the future of AI-driven creativity

What you’ll need

  • Genuine curiosity about AI video, world models, agentic engineering and generative media and an intuition for how to design meaningful interactions with these systems

  • Experience designing flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity UIs for web and agentic products

  • Experience building agentic tools or interfaces — i.e., systems where AI takes actions, reasons over state, or drives multi-step workflows

  • Strong understanding of visual and interaction design, as well as usability testing

  • Comfort working in ambiguous, research oriented environments where the problem space is still being defined

  • Strong understanding of visual and interaction design, as well as usability testing.

  • Solid graphic design fundamentals — typography, layout, color — applied to high-converting ad formats, not just editorial or brand work

jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

Open to hiring remote — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

Runway is hiring a Detection & Response Engineer to own how we find and stop attacks against our infrastructure, our research environment and our products.

Securing a company that trains and serves frontier video models is a different problem from securing a typical SaaS product. The environment includes research compute, large training datasets, a fast-moving build pipeline and engineers who work inside AI-assisted tooling every day. Each of those changes what an attack looks like and what you need to see to catch it.

You'll join the Security team and build our detection and response program the way an engineer would: detections as code, response as automation, evidence as something you can query. This is a role with real ownership: you'll own the detection program end to end, from what we log to how quickly we close an incident. You'll report to the head of security, partner with engineers across platform and research, and shape how this function grows from here.

What you'll do

  • Own detection and response end to end: what we log, what we alert on, how we triage and how we recover

  • Write and tune detections as code across multiple cloud environments, Kubernetes, identity systems, endpoints and SaaS, and measure them on coverage and precision rather than alert volume

  • Lead incident response from the first alert through containment and forensics, then write the post-incident review people actually read

  • Build automation that takes toil out of triage, including enrichment, correlation, containment actions and evidence collection, and use LLM-based tooling where it holds up under audit

  • Monitor AI agents and developer tooling operating inside our environment, and turn that into concrete telemetry and controls

  • Partner with platform and research engineers so new systems ship with logging and response playbooks in place on day one

  • Run threat hunts and tabletop exercises against the parts of the environment that worry you most, and fix what you find

  • Turn incident and detection metrics into evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001 and enterprise customer security reviews, working with our GRC team

  • Participate in an on-call rotation for security incidents

What you'll need

  • Hands-on incident response experience: you've triaged live alerts, led investigations and written up what happened afterward

  • Experience building and tuning detections in a modern SIEM, ideally managed as code

  • Working knowledge of how attackers move through cloud and Kubernetes environments (IAM abuse, container escape, credential theft, supply chain compromise) and what that leaves behind in logs

  • Comfort writing Python, Typescript, Rust or another language to automate response work and connect security tools

  • Familiarity with at least one major cloud platform and with Kubernetes at the level of audit logs, RBAC and workload identity

  • Clear writing. Incident timelines, detection documentation and updates to leadership are all part of the job

  • Judgment about what to alert on, what to automate and when to wake someone up

Even better if you have

  • Experience monitoring GPU or HPC-style infrastructure, or research environments with large datasets

  • Experience building detections or guardrails for AI agents, LLM tooling or MCP servers

  • Cloud forensics experience: disk and memory acquisition, cloud audit trail reconstruction, chain of custody

  • Published open source detection content

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

*Preferable to have someone near one of our offices in NYC or San Francisco, but open to hiring around the world for the right candidate.

Runway Enterprise is a complete solution for enterprises, offering out-of-the-box creative tools, a generative media developer platform, model licensing, and forward-deployed creatives and researchers that embed directly within enterprises.

We're hiring an Enterprise product marketing leader for Runway Enterprise, leading the segment and developing priority verticals including Media, Retail/eCommerce, Software, and more.

This is not a purely positioning or “launch” role. You'll own the success of the enterprise segment, partnering closely with the sales & enablement team, enterprise marketing & growth. You’ll lead the development of Runway’s overall enterprise messaging and positioning and create tailored, vertical-specific messages and value propositions, built from your first-hand experiences engaging directly with Runway’s customers.

This is a builder's role. You'll be defining the discipline, working shoulder-to-shoulder with sales, product, creative, marketing and growth; you'll be measured on the growth of the business (not just on assets shipped or messaging consistency).

What You'll Do

  • Own the Enterprise segment. Define Runway audiences in the enterprise: who they are, the jobs they hire Runway for, how they differ across verticals. Ground audiences in hands on customer research, win/loss details, and usage analysis. Turn these insights into a point of view that product and leadership actually build against.

  • Own positioning and messaging for enterprise & vertical solutions. Define how Runway is positioned across its audiences, with tight value propositions and proof points for key verticals. You’ll make the story sharp, consistent, and reflective of Runway's ambitious brand, and make sure a professional buyer recognizes themselves in it.

  • Drive acquisition and conversion, not just awareness. Partner with growth to move the funnel that matters for this segment: acquisition channels and targeting that find more customers within our ICPs. You're comfortable owning metrics and running experiments, not just producing the narrative around them.

  • Drive competitive intelligence and response. Track and deeply understand the key players across the AI creative tools market. Turn your market understanding into a living point of view on where we win, where we're exposed, and how we respond, and make it legible to product and leadership.

  • Partner on enablement. Partner with the sales enablement team to develop assets that drive confidence in Runway’s customers and sellers alike.

  • Player & coach. You’ll operate hands on as the direct owner of Enterprise and Solutions Marketing; opportunity to lead and manage a team of PMMs for candidates of the right seniority.

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years in product marketing, including time leading PMM for a winning enterprise product at meaningful scale. You’ll bring a track record of work that moved business metrics and grew new verticals (not just launches & messaging that you shipped).

  • Core & Vertical expertise. You’re comfortable leading product positioning exercises at the executive level. You come with a proven track record of industry/vertical product marketing, including defining, developing, and launching new verticals.

  • Exceptional positioning and narrative craft. You can take research concepts and technical products and make them land for a discerning, professional audience. You create sharp positioning, ad creative, and launch stories (and you can write them yourself).

  • You thrive in an environment with rapid pace and a high accountability culture. You move very fast, make decisions with incomplete information, and instinctively gravitate toward shipping today (not writing docs for tomorrow).

  • Sharp competitive instincts. You track markets closely, form a real point of view on where to win, and translate it into product and messaging decisions.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You confidently assess the state of the business, call out challenges, and articulate your plans to solve them.

  • (Bonus) Pricing and packaging experience. You've shaped how a product is packaged and priced across individual and team/enterprise tiers, and you understand the tradeoffs a self-serve-to-enterprise motion creates.

  • (Bonus) PLG. You've led product marketing efforts in a growth stage company with both PLG & Sales Led motions.

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team responsible for Runway's product platform and API. You should have experience growing high-performing engineering teams and be deeply interested in the intersection of product development, APIs, and distributed systems. You will will manage our current and growing team of 5.

You’ll have a chance to work closely with our product engineering, product management, and finance teams to build low-latency, high-reliability APIs for our AI-powered creation tools as well as the infrastructure to support them.

A peek at our technical stack

Our API endpoints for real-time collaboration and media asset management is written in TypeScript, and runs in ECS containers on AWS Fargate. We leverage multiple AWS-native components, such as S3, CloudFront, Lambda, Kinesis, and SQS, as building blocks of our infrastructure.

Our inference backend is written in Python (PyTorch, TorchScript), and is deployed across multiple clusters / cloud providers. We use Kubernetes for container orchestration, and k8s-native components such as Flyte, Kueue, and Kyverno efficient job orchestration. We invest in prometheus and grafana for monitoring, and Terraform to manage our infrastructure.

What you’ll do 

  • Drive platform strategy and architecture for our TypeScript-based API infrastructure, ensuring code quality, maintainability, and scalability as we grow

  • Own the public API domain end-to-end, from technical architecture to revenue growth, ensuring it's a high-quality, revenue-generating platform that developers love

  • Manage our data and analytics infrastructure, ensuring data integrity, security, and accessibility for teams across the company

  • Lead and grow a team of 4-6 platform engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement

  • Partner with Product Engineering teams to unblock new feature launches, providing platform support and ensuring smooth integration between frontend experiences and backend capabilities

  • Own critical data pipelines and metrics that power business decisions across Finance (cost-of-sales, revenue attribution), Support (usage analytics, error tracking), and Product (feature adoption, performance metrics)

  • Work cross-functionally with leadership to set priorities, communicate progress, and align platform investments with business goals

What you’ll need

  • 2+ years of experience in an engineering manager or team lead role, with a track record of building and scaling high-performing teams

  • 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience, with specific expertise operating TypeScript services in the cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure)

  • Strong product sensibility and business acumen – you understand how technical decisions impact revenue, customer satisfaction, and company metrics

  • Experience owning revenue-generating platforms or products, with an understanding of API economics, usage-based pricing, and developer experience

  • Solid foundation in data engineering and analytics, including experience with metrics pipelines, data modeling, and business intelligence tooling

  • Database expertise, particularly in managing production databases at scale, data migrations, and ensuring data integrity

  • Excellent cross-functional communication skills – you can translate technical concepts for business teams, explain business constraints to engineers, and build consensus across diverse stakeholders

  • Comfort with ambiguity and rapid iteration – you can make smart trade-offs between perfect and good-enough in a fast-moving startup environment

  • Empathetic and inclusive leadership style that empowers engineers to do their best work

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

jobs.title: GTM Engineer
jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

Open to hiring remote across the US. We also have offices in NYC, San Francisco and Seattle.

This is the builder seat on the revenue team. You'll spend your time with sellers (BDRs, AEs and account managers), learning where the motion breaks. Then you'll fix it with software: signals, scoring, routing, agents and the CRM underneath. In practice you're also our RevOps lead, so you own the systems that turn product usage into pipeline and pipeline into closed-won.

At Runway, a GTM Engineer understands the rep's day as well as the stack. You know why a lead should be worked now, which account deserves an AE's afternoon, and what gets a rep to actually open a tool. Then you build it with Clay, SQL, APIs and agentic workflows, where a traditional ops hire would file a ticket or buy another tool. We care more about what you've shipped and the behavior it changed than about the title you held.

What you'll do

Signal, scoring & pipeline

  • Design our account and lead scoring model, with Fit, Intent and Engagement as separate inputs, and keep it honest against conversion data

  • Build the PLG-to-Enterprise signal layer: product usage, web and third-party intent feeding a prioritized BDR/AE queue, with routing and SLAs reps trust

  • Turn every signal into a reason to reach out (why this account, why now, why this person), packaged so a rep can act in minutes

  • Own Clay enrichment and outbound data infrastructure, and raise BDR output at the systems level

  • Spot patterns in what converts (segments, use cases, messaging, timing) and bring them to Sales, Marketing and Product

Seller workflow & agents

  • Sit with frontline sellers to find where the motion breaks, then ship the fix within two weeks

  • Build and run the GTM agent fleet (account research, pre-call briefs, follow-up drafts, CRM updates) from prototype to daily use, with reps reviewing and approving

  • Surface the right account context at the right moment: before QBRs, ahead of renewals, when an expansion signal fires

  • Build churn-risk and expansion detection with Deployment and CX so the post-sale motion runs on live signals

  • Instrument every agent so decisions, failures, human edits and outcomes are visible, and own the loop of evals and iteration

Revenue systems & policy

  • Own the commercial model in Salesforce (routing, territories, rules of engagement, approvals) as the source every system and agent reads from

  • Connect the stack (Salesforce, Gong, Clay, product usage, the warehouse) so an account looks the same everywhere

  • Automate deal desk work: quote workflows, discount approval routing, and pricing guardrails enforced in-system

  • Partner with Sales leadership and Finance on comp plan and policy mechanics (crediting, CRM hygiene requirements, win/loss capture), and build systems that make the behavior we pay for the easy path

  • Build the reporting under the CRO dashboard: pipeline coverage, conversion rates, ramp velocity, forecast accuracy

Measurement & iteration

  • Own every build end to end: discovery, prototype, rollout, adoption, iteration

About the role

*Open to candidates based near our NYC office or those willing to relocate.

We're looking for a Workplace Lead to own Runway's offices: where they are, how they get built and how they feel to work in.

Today that means New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, & Tel Aviv. Over the next few years it means more room in those cities and new locations elsewhere. You'll handle the real estate and the buildouts, what it costs to run each site, and the events and visits that happen in these rooms. You'll work with cross functional partners including People and Finance on how much space we need and when, and with IT and Security on what it takes to make a site usable.

Expect to be close to the work itself, not only the strategy behind it. Things are always moving quickly at Runway, so this role calls for exceptional organization and the judgment to know what needs a plan and what just needs doing.

What you’ll do

  • Handle the daily operation of each office: cleaning, repairs, food, supplies, access control, and health and safety

  • Own the workplace budget and the reporting behind it, from rent and capex through daily operating spend

  • Run Runway's onsite programming, including all-hands, offsites, team events, screenings and visits from partners and press

  • Decide how much space Runway needs in each city and by when, working from hiring forecasts with People and Finance

  • Take new offices from shortlist to signed lease, working with brokers, Legal and Finance on terms

  • Manage design, construction and furniture projects to move-in dates that hold

  • Work with IT and Security on network, AV and physical access ahead of each opening

  • Set up local vendors, services and compliance in markets where Runway hasn't operated before

  • Travel occasionally to Runway's other offices, usually around an opening or a large onsite event

  • Decide what good looks like for a Runway office, then keep checking each one against it, from the perspective of both the people working there and the people visiting

What you’ll need

  • 7+ years in corporate real estate, facilities or workplace operations

  • Deep project management experience across construction schedules, permitting and short-notice logistics

  • Hands-on lease and vendor contract experience, and a budget you personally signed off on

  • Cross-functional experience with teams such as Finance, People, IT and Security

  • At least one office you took from first site visit through opening day

  • Comfort writing the process docs, service standards and vendor scorecards a workplace function depends on

  • Accountability for offices you don't sit in every day

About the role

*Open to hiring remote — we also have offices in New York, San Francisco, Seattle, London, Paris, and Tel Aviv.

Runway is hiring an Infrastructure Security Engineer to secure the platform our models are trained and served on. The role covers Kubernetes platform security, cloud identity and access, software supply chain, tenant isolation in the serving layer and the research infrastructure behind our models.

Securing a company that trains and serves frontier video models is a different problem from securing a typical SaaS product. The environment includes research compute, large training datasets, a fast-moving build pipeline, and engineers who work inside AI-assisted tooling every day. Each of those changes what an attack looks like and what the platform has to enforce to stop it.

This is a hands-on engineering role on the Security team. You'll write policy, tooling and infrastructure code, work in the platform team's repositories, and ship controls that hold up in production.

What you'll do

  • Design and ship security controls in our Kubernetes ecosystem: admission policy, RBAC, workload identity, network policy and runtime hardening across every cluster we run

  • Harden the software supply chain from dependency intake through build and deploy, including package firewalling, artifact signing and provenance, and admission controls that block what doesn't pass

  • Own cloud IAM and identity architecture: least-privilege roles, short-lived credentials and workload federation

  • Secure research infrastructure and training pipelines, including access to model weights and datasets, without slowing down the people using them

  • Threat model new platform components before they ship and turn the findings into concrete requirements the owning team can act on

  • Build guardrails for AI agents and developer tooling operating inside our infrastructure

  • Write infrastructure as code and policy as code, and treat security configuration with the same review and rollout discipline as any other change

  • Give the incident response team what they need when infrastructure is involved: fast answers about how a system works and what to shut off

What you'll need

  • Hands-on experience securing Kubernetes in production: you've written admission policies, debugged RBAC and workload identity problems and understand how a cluster gets compromised

  • Working knowledge of cloud IAM and networking on at least one major cloud platform, including how identity federation and short-lived credentials actually work

  • Experience with infrastructure as code and GitOps-style deployment, and the habit of shipping security changes through the same pipeline as everything else

  • Comfort writing Python, Typescript, Rust or another language to build tooling, not just scripts

  • An understanding of software supply chain attacks and the controls that stop them: signing, provenance, SBOMs, admission enforcement

  • Clear writing. Design docs, threat models and explanations to engineers who don't work in security are all part of the job

  • Judgment about which controls to enforce, which to recommend and how to roll out a breaking change without breaking the company

Even better if you have

  • Experience securing GPU or HPC-style compute, training pipelines or research environments

  • Experience with policy engines and admission controllers (Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper, Falco or similar)

  • Multi-tenant isolation design in a cloud environment: ABAC, scoped credentials, per-tenant boundaries

  • Experience producing security architecture evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001 or other audits and customer assessments

  • Open source contributions or published work in cloud or Kubernetes security

*Open to hiring remote across the US and Canada — we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, and Seattle

We are growing our commercial team and looking for growth-minded leaders who are passionate about the future of AI and content creation. As our first leader within Sales Development, you will build and scale our founding BDR organization.

This role is equal parts people leadership and systems building. You’ll directly manage and develop our early BDR team (currently two people) while building the infrastructure, processes, and outbound strategies that define the future of prospecting at Runway. We’re not looking to replicate traditional SDR playbooks — we want someone excited to rethink sales development through AI-powered workflows, automation, product signals, and highly personalized outreach, while helping shape how Runway wins in the enterprise market.

What you’ll do

  • Lead, mentor, and grow Runway’s founding BDR team, creating a high-performance culture centered around curiosity, experimentation, and continuous improvement

  • Build the systems, processes, and infrastructure that power a modern AI-first sales development organization

  • Define how AI tooling, automation, and human creativity work together across outbound prospecting, research, personalization, and pipeline generation

  • Turn product usage signals, API activity, and inbound demand into scalable enterprise opportunity generation workflows

  • Develop highly targeted, vertical-specific outbound motions aligned to Runway’s evolving use cases and customer needs

  • Continuously test and refine messaging, sequencing, workflows, and enablement programs to improve team effectiveness

  • Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Creative, and RevOps to shape ICP strategy, lead routing, and overall GTM execution

  • Work alongside sales leadership to help define and scale Runway’s enterprise sales motion

What you’ll need

  • 5+ years of experience in sales, growth, or GTM leadership roles

  • Experience managing and developing high-performing SDR/ BDR teams

  • Strong systems-thinking mindset with experience building outbound processes and operational infrastructure from the ground up

  • Deep interest in AI-native workflows and a strong point of view on how AI will reshape modern prospecting and sales development

  • Experience operating in product-led, usage-based, or highly technical GTM environments

  • Highly analytical and data-driven, with the ability to use insights to drive strategy and execution

  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and excited to experiment and iterate quickly

  • Strong communicator and cross-functional collaborator with a builder mentality

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

About the Role

Runway is looking for a Marketing Manager to help build and scale high-impact marketing programs across our creator, partner, sponsorship, and growth ecosystem.

This is a generalist marketing role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. Some immediate areas of focus include influencer creator partnerships, sponsorships, and partnership marketing.

The right person is commercially minded, highly organized, creative, and comfortable operating in ambiguity. We are looking for someone who can build repeatable programs, manage relationships, and execute campaigns to turn marketing ideas into measurable growth.

What You’ll Do

  • You will own and support marketing programs that help Runway reach priority audiences, grow demand, and deepen our presence among our target audiences.

  • In the near term, this will include managing creator and influencer partnerships including affiliates, evaluating sponsorship opportunities, and building co-marketing programs with customers, technology partners, model providers, vendors, and ecosystem partners.

  • You will work across the full program lifecycle: identifying opportunities, developing briefs, managing outreach, coordinating execution, tracking performance, and recommending what to scale, change, or stop.

  • You will partner closely with growth, creative, comms, events, PMM, sales, business development, legal, and finance to make sure programs are clear, on-brand, operationally sound, and connected to business outcomes.

What We’re Looking For

  • We’re looking for a marketing generalist with strong executional judgment and enough strategic range to work across multiple types of programs for a range of B2C and B2B audiences.

  • Experience managing creator partnerships with a clear view of how long-form content performs differently from short-form and other social channels.

  • 4+ years of experience building marketing campaigns, influencer, affiliate, or growth programs from 0 to 1.

  • Experience managing external relationships: creators, sponsors, agencies, freelancers or vendors.

  • Experience writing briefs, managing timelines, coordinating stakeholders, and translating broad goals into concrete plans.

  • Strong taste, communication skills, and judgment around brand, audience fit, creator quality, partner value, business impact, and operational tradeoffs.

  • You should be comfortable with ambiguity and able to build from scratch. This role requires someone who can create structure where it does not yet exist, but without slowing the team down with unnecessary process.

  • You should care about measurement and be able to connect marketing programs to outcomes such as subscriptions, ARR, and enterprise pipeline influence.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in AI, SaaS, subscription products.

  • Experience creating partner-facing materials such as briefs, sponsorship packages, or co-marketing materials.

  • Familiarity with Runway, AI video, creator communities, internet culture, and the broader creative technology ecosystem.

jobs.title: Member of Applied AI Team
jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

Why this matters

Runway is building AI to simulate the world. We think world models, not language models alone, are the path to general-purpose simulation: systems that experience the world, learn from their mistakes, and change how stories get told, how science gets done, and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Applied AI is where that research meets a customer with a deadline. Every one of the world's largest studios, brands, and platforms hits a moment where Runway stops being a demo and becomes the way they actually make things. Our team exists for that moment, and we organize around one question: what's blocking this customer from production, and how do we remove it?

About the role

This is a role for people who want to own a problem, not an account. You'll sit with the biggest studios, brands, and Fortune 100 companies in the world, figure out what's actually standing between them and production, and build whatever removes it. Some weeks that's a workflow. Some weeks it's a plugin or an integration nobody has written yet. Some weeks it's getting a room of executives to make a decision they've been putting off.

Your work will be on screen: Emmy-winning shows, Oscar-winning films, Super Bowl commercials, the stuff people actually watch. And the things you build for one customer tend to become product for all of them. Our team's first Shopify plugin started as a customer blocker and was in engineering's hands within a few weeks. We treat this team as R&D for that reason, not as a cost center.

We have offices in NYC, San Francisco, Seattle, and London.

No two weeks are the same, but you can expect to:

  • Find the real problem: sit with the creative, technical, and executive teams at a customer, map how they actually work, and locate the blocker between them and production. Usually it's one of three things: a missing integration, an unproven pipeline, or a stakeholder who isn't convinced yet.

  • Build the first of its kind: the demo that shows a studio head or a Fortune 100 CMO something nobody has shown them before. Working proofs of concept on the customer's own brand, footage, or catalog, often built in a day or two before the meeting, and the best of them become product for everyone.

  • Make it reusable: turn the one-off that unblocked one customer into the workflow, plugin, or integration the next ten customers start from.

  • Run the evaluation: own evaluation plans end to end, guide managed trials, build tailored demos on the customer's own footage and brand, and carry the technical side of deal cycles with AEs.

  • Scope deployments that land: 4–12 week engagements with customer-defined success criteria, a hands-on builder and an executive sponsor on their side from day one, and enough discipline to keep them on scope when the asks start piling up.

  • Get customers to production fast: take new technical and non-technical customers from signed contract to first production call in days rather than quarters, grow API-only accounts into Platform + API, and fix the onboarding so the support tickets stop coming.

  • Present to anyone: walk an analyst through a pipeline in the morning and a studio head through a production plan in the afternoon.

  • Bring the field back to the product: embed with Product, Engineering, and Creative to turn what you saw at the customer into roadmap. Every repeat ask is a product requirement, not a patch.

  • Measure what the customer measures: time to production, usage before and after a project, what they shipped because you were there. We track our own numbers in Salesforce and the warehouse; you'll own yours.

What we value

  • People who aren't satisfied with surface-level answers and will go into the data, the code, and the room to find the real one

  • Low ego: the customer's outcome matters more than who gets the credit

  • Comfort with open-ended problems in unstructured environments, and the instinct to create structure instead of waiting for it

  • Builders who would rather prototype than debate, and who keep iterating with the customer until it actually works

  • Adaptive and introspective: willing to learn, guide, lead, and follow

What we need

  • You build things that run in production. Python or TypeScript, APIs, integrations, and data pipelines. Whether you write the code yourself or with coding agents, you can read it, debug it when it breaks, and explain line by line why it's built that way, including to a customer's engineering team. You've shipped something a customer actually ran: a workflow, an integration, a plugin, or an internal tool.

  • You've deployed AI or ML systems and integrations inside complex organizations and can point to the outcome, not just the delivery

  • You can hold a room of executives and a room of engineers, and translate between the two. Some of those rooms are at the customer, so expect some travel.

  • Nice to have: data tooling (SQL, BigQuery, Retool), or experience in media, entertainment, or advertising production

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

Working at Runway

We’re committed to creating a space where our employees can bring their full selves to work and have equal opportunity to succeed. So regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, origin, ability, age, veteran status, if joining this mission speaks to you, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Member of Product Staff, Agents
jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.

World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.

Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

Preferable to have someone near an office in NYC or San Francisco, but open to hiring around the world for the right candidate.

Runway Creative is an all-in-one platform giving creators and businesses endless ways to generate and edit video, images, and audio. Our user base spans across professional creatives, as well as business owners and enterprise marketing and merchandising teams that come to Runway to generate videos, ads and other content to promote their products and services.

We're hiring for a Senior Product Manager to build agent products. You’ll own new product development end-to-end, from customer and technical discovery, to product shaping and viability, to quality and feedback loops that make these products better. You’ll work at the frontier of agentic product development, shaping how Runway Agents help our customers grow their businesses.

What you’ll do

  • Represent the customer: develop deep understanding of creative and marketing workflows through frequent customer engagement; synthesize findings on agent performance and behavior, and lead a team with clarity and conviction.

  • Lead Agent Development: run user interviews, competitive research, eval analysis, and prompt experimentation. Shape your findings into new product offerings that solve customer problems in new and novel ways.

  • Own agent quality: create eval infrastructure, monitor regressions, and ensure that agents improves with every release.

  • Shape the scope: scope ruthlessly to deliver exceptional user value on a fast paced release.

  • Ship, hands-on. ship your own PRs to improve the product experience. You'll be in the details daily and shipping regularly.

  • Create compelling launch moments: enable sales, support, and marketing with the context they need to communicate new agent capabilities effectively

What you’ll need

  • 8+ years in the software industry, with direct ownership of an AI or LLM powered product in a product management or engineering leadership role. A track record of moving revenue and adoption metrics, not just shipping features.

  • You thrive in an environment with rapid pace and a high accountability culture. You move very fast, make decisions with incomplete information, and instinctively gravitate towards shipping today, not writing docs for tomorrow.

  • Hands-on experience building and shipping agent-products - you understand tool use, planning loops, multi-step reasoning, and how and why agents fail. You have deep familiarity with prompt engineering and evaluation frameworks.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication. You can make a sharp, written argument and tell a compelling launch story. You confidently assess the state of the business, call out challenges and articulate your plans to solve them.

Runway strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on competitive market rates for our size, stage and industry, and salary is just one part of the overall compensation package we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

jobs.description_html:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.

We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery.
