jobs.title: Strategist, Agent Development - Retail
jobs.description_html:
About us

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

About the Retail team

  • Sierra is partnering with a large and growing number of retailers - spanning apparel and beauty, grocery and big-box, home and auto, consumer services, marketplaces, and consumer technology. Our agents help millions of shoppers and members every day: tracking and returning orders, finding the right product, booking services, and resolving issues in each brand’s own voice.

  • Retail is also where AI agents go beyond support to generate revenue. From product discovery and personalized recommendations to cart recovery, win-back campaigns, and in-store support that turns unanswered store calls into visits and sales, our team is redefining what an agent can do for a brand’s top line - not just its cost line.

  • Join us to transform how the world’s most-loved consumer brands engage their customers - and help build technology that makes shopping more personal, effortless, and delightful for everyone.

What you’ll do

As an Agent Strategist, you own how Sierra’s AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. You transform a customer’s thorniest, highest-stakes problems into agents that measurably move their business.

  • Own the Agent Development Life Cycle. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it’s the best version of itself in the real world. You’ll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

  • Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers’ executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

  • Partner with the customer’s working teams day to day. Run working sessions, troubleshoot the agent as issues come up, and make the calls that keep the build on track for launch.

  • Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.

Example projects

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

  • Launch an order management agent for a national apparel brand — order lookup, cancellations, returns, and exchanges — then hill-climb containment and CSAT week over week.

  • Partner with Product to build a shopping agent that plugs into a retailer’s existing search and recommendation systems to guide product discovery — turning the support channel into a revenue channel.

  • Stand up an in-store support voice agent for a big-box or grocery retailer, answering the stock-check and store-info calls that largely go unanswered today and converting them into store visits and sales.

  • Design a booking, payments, and outbound agent for a consumer services brand operating hundreds of locations.

  • Help a marketplace handle order status and buyer–seller disputes at enormous scale.

  • Launch outbound campaigns — cart recovery, win-back, churn saves, and subscription renewals — across voice and SMS.

What you’ll bring

  • Customer obsession. Genuine energy being in front of customers — understanding their business and needs, thriving in complex organizations, and building trusted relationships.

  • Communication. Clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strategic problem-solving in ambiguity. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to break down complex problems, spot risks early, and adapt as things change fast.

  • Technical aptitude. Comfortable engaging directly with technical concepts - reading API documentation, understanding data models and system architecture, and following engineering tradeoffs in a design discussion.

  • Ownership and delivery. A track record of running multiple complex, high-visibility projects at once and driving them to outcomes.

  • Interest in retail and consumer experiences. Experience in e-commerce, retail technology, marketplaces, or consumer brands — and familiarity with commerce and CX stacks (e.g., commerce platforms, order management systems, contact center software) — is a strong plus.

Even better...

  • Experience building or deploying AI/LLM agents in production — hands-on with the tools behind them (eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering) — working closely with technical counterparts.

  • You’ve been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience — and/or an MBA or comparable experience at the intersection of technology and business.

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

  • Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

  • Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

  • Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

  • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

  • Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

  • Life insurance and disability benefits

  • Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

  • Parental leave

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

  • Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

  • Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

jobs.title: Strategist, Agent Development - Travel, Transportation and Hospitality
jobs.description_html:
About us

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

About the Travel, Transportation and Hospitality team

  • The Travel, Transportation and Hospitality (TTH) supports some of the largest airlines, hotel chains, rental car brands, cruise lines and travel tech companies in the world. Our customers are pioneers in the travel space and are true thought partners in shaping our platform, helping reinvent what hospitality looks like in this new era. Our customers rely on us not only to deliver exceptional customer experiences, but also to drive meaningful growth for their businesses.

  • Our TTH team is constantly pushing the bounds of what is possible within this industry and beyond. We help support our customers in the moments that matter — whether that’s proactively encouraging new bookings to prepare for exciting events, or helping guests rebook their flights or stays during times of distress. We help our customers maximize the lifetime value of their guests and build products to delight guests at every touchpoint.

  • We’re a small and scrappy team, and we support each other with any deliverables we have to meet. Every engineer on TTH is also a product-led thinker; every PM on TTH is tinkering and developing tangible prototypes; and every strategist on TTH is capable of owning an agent end to end. As a part of this team, you’ll set the standard for what it means to go beyond your role, and help build the travel industry of the future.

What you’ll do

As an Agent Strategist, you own how Sierra’s AI agents come to life for our customers — from first pilot to a production agent handling thousands of conversations a day. You sit at the intersection of product, building agents and customer-facing work, and stay just as close to the technology as you are to the people you build for. You transform a customer’s thorniest, highest-stakes problems into agents that measurably move their business.

  • Own the Agent Development Life Cycle. Take agents from initial scope through conversation design, tooling, and evaluation, to launch and continuous iteration in production — translating business goals into an agent that outperforms, and tuning relentlessly until it’s the best version of itself in the real world. You’ll have real ownership and autonomy over the outcome.

  • Be the trusted strategic advisor to enterprise leaders. Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with our customers’ executives, understand what success actually means to their business, and shape the AI strategy that gets them there.

  • Partner with the customer’s working teams day to day. Run working sessions, troubleshoot the agent as issues come up, and make the calls that keep the build on track for launch.

  • Directly impact product. Surface unmet needs from your customer work, and feed them back to research and platform to shape where Sierra goes next.

Example projects

These are the kinds of projects that strategists on our team have worked on recently:

  • Scope and launch a subscription-retention agent for a large telecommunications or media company that consistently outperforms human agents at saving at-risk customers.

  • Stand up an agent for a commerce customer that troubleshoots a broken device end-to-end and personalizes product recommendations in the same conversation.

  • Redesign the conversation flows for a financial services agent so it can handle complex, regulated interactions — and convert a pilot into a multi-team production deployment. See our financial services blog for examples.

  • Partner with product on a net-new capability — a new agent architecture or self-service tooling — using a live customer as the design partner.

  • Define the evaluation and quality bar for a new agent, then use those metrics to drive a measurable lift in outcome week over week.

What you’ll bring

  • Customer obsession. Genuine energy being in front of customers — understanding their business and needs, thriving in complex organizations, and building trusted relationships.

  • Communication. Clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Strategic problem-solving in ambiguity. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills to break down complex problems, spot risks early, and adapt as things change fast.

  • Technical aptitude. Comfortable engaging directly with technical concepts - reading API documentation, understanding data models and system architecture, and following engineering tradeoffs in a design discussion.

  • Ownership and delivery. A track record of running multiple complex, high-visibility projects at once and driving them to outcomes.

Even better...

  • Experience building or deploying AI/LLM agents in production — hands-on with the tools behind them (eval frameworks, agent tooling, RAG, prompt engineering) — working closely with technical counterparts.

  • You’ve been a founder, founding team member, or operator — you know how to balance craft, ownership, and speed.

  • A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience — and/or an MBA or comparable experience at the intersection of technology and business.

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

  • Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

  • Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

  • Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

  • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

  • Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

  • Life insurance and disability benefits

  • Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

  • Parental leave

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

  • Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

  • Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead full-cycle recruitment processes, from sourcing and screening to closing and onboarding, ensuring a seamless and positive candidate experience.

  • Identify and engage with passive candidates through various channels, including online platforms, networking events, and industry connections, to build a strong, diverse talent pipeline.

  • Drive initiatives to ensure diverse hiring practices and build a team reflective of our values and culture.

  • Utilize metrics and analytics to track recruiting performance, identify areas for improvement, and optimize processes to achieve hiring targets, reporting regularly to hiring partners.

  • Develop and execute our campus recruiting strategy, building relationships with universities and student communities, and representing Sierra on campus through recruiting events, career fairs, and other programs that build awareness and attract exceptional early-career talent.

  • Help build and run Sierra’s internship and early-career programs, from campus recruiting and events to creating a high-quality intern experience that engages, develops, and converts exceptional early talent.

What You'll Bring:

  • 5+ years of full-cycle or university recruiting experience, preferably in a fast-paced, high-growth tech environment.

  • Proven ability to develop and execute recruiting strategies that align with business objectives.

  • Proficiency in using recruiting metrics and data to inform decisions and improve processes.

  • Strong collaboration skills with a willingness to work cross-functionally to achieve Sierra’s goals.

  • Relationships with career centers, student orgs, faculty, and ambassadors.

  • Experience in planning and executing campus engagement strategies, across universities through targeted events and partnerships.

Even better...

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity in order to adapt to the ever-changing needs of a growing organization.

  • Ability and willingness to travel during peak recruiting cycles and work flexible hours as needed

  • An interest in building from the ground up: launching intern programs, designing early talent hiring process

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

  • Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

  • Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

  • Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

  • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

  • Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

  • Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

  • Life insurance and disability benefits

  • Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

  • Parental leave

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized 

  • Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

  • Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. We strive to evaluate all applicants consistently without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

  • Own frontend across product and marketing surfaces: You will work across both our core product interface and customer-facing web pages, ensuring a cohesive, polished user experience across all touch points. This includes building features in the web app and also collaborating on our website to keep branding and user experience consistent and high-quality.

  • Build content infrastructure that unblocks the team: You'll develop our CMS (we use Sanity) to give content and marketing teams self-serve tooling, structured content models, and preview/staging workflows, so routine changes don't depend on engineering. You'll design content schemas and editing experiences that let non-engineers move quickly and confidently.

  • Champion growth: You'll partner with marketing, sales, and operations to implement analytics and enable experimentation, turning business goals into shipped, instrumented features so we always know what's actually working.

  • Make localization first-class: You'll support localization and internationalization — multilingual content, translation workflows, and the infrastructure behind them, so non-English experiences are genuinely first-class rather than afterthoughts.

  • Treat performance as a feature: You'll own Core Web Vitals, media and asset optimization, and the diagnosis of the subtle issues: layout shift, lazy-loading, video quality, render timing. You care about speed, and you measure it.

  • Hold a high bar for accessibility: You'll champion semantic markup, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and WCAG-minded component design, ensuring the site is usable by everyone who visits it.

What you'll bring

  • Marketing and growth fluency: You've worked on marketing or growth-facing web before, and you understand the business context — funnels, conversion, SEO, analytics, and A/B testing—not just the code. We care about this more than years of experience or exact seniority.

  • Strong frontend fundamentals: You're fluent in modern JavaScript and TypeScript and React (or a similar framework), with a real sense for UI/UX craft and an instinct for getting the small details right.

  • A genuine commitment to performance and accessibility: You care about both deeply and can point to specific, concrete things you've done to improve them in production.

  • Comfort with structured content: You've worked with a headless CMS and structured content models before. Sanity experience is a plus.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration: You work well with non-engineers — designers, content writers, and marketers — and can translate their goals into technical work, and technical tradeoffs back into terms they can act on.

Even better...

  • Localization and i18n experience: You've worked with internationalization systems and translation tooling before.

  • Analytics and experimentation depth: You're familiar with web analytics and experimentation platforms and know how to use them to drive decisions.

  • Third-party integration experience: You've integrated services like video hosting or error monitoring into a content workflow.

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful.   • Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

  • Life insurance and disability benefits

  • Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

  • Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized

jobs.title: Accounting Manager
jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

As one of the first hires on Suno's accounting team you'll be a true generalist, the person who can pick up whatever the close, the auditors, or the business throws your way and run with it. Reporting to the Director of Accounting, you'll own meaningful pieces of the monthly close, help carry the company through its first-year audit and toward IPO readiness, and bring a measured, meaningful approach to AI that unlocks the efficiency expected of a best-in-class team. We're looking for a doer who wants to build: someone who'll set up a process, document it, operate it, and then automate it. If you want broad exposure and the chance to shape how a fast-growing AI company does its accounting, this is the seat.

Listen to the song we made about the role: https://suno.com/s/sFjswHv402TX3Yeo

What You'll Do

  • Own significant areas of the monthly close, reconciliations, accruals, and journal entries, and help shorten and tighten the cycle.

  • Build and document repeatable processes across the accounting function, balancing startup flexibility with the rigor the business needs.

  • Support the company's first-year financial statement audit and help build toward the rigor required for IPO readiness.

  • Research technical accounting questions and support audit and tax requests with well-organized workpapers and analysis.

  • Put AI and automation to work across the accounting function, thoughtfully and with the right guardrails, to unlock the efficiency expected of a best-in-class team.

  • Strengthen a growing accounting team's foundation across process and systems so we can keep making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone.

What You'll Need

Must-Haves

  • 5-7 years of accounting experience, including a mix of Big 4 public accounting and high-growth industry.

  • Strong US GAAP knowledge and a track record of owning core close responsibilities end to end.

  • Experience supporting external financial statement audits, first-year audit experience is ideal.

  • A generalist's range, comfortable moving between technical accounting, operational accounting, and systems work.

  • A demonstrated, measured use of AI and automation to make accounting faster and more accurate.

  • Builder's energy and the judgment to know when to apply rigor and when to stay flexible in a startup.

Nice-to-Haves

  • CPA.

  • Consumer tech or other high-volume revenue experience.

  • Exposure to music royalties, equity, indirect tax, or payroll accounting.

  • IPO readiness or SOX experience.

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • Willingness to travel (up to 10%) to collaborate with team members across Suno office locations.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Compensation

The annual base salary range for this role is $142,000 – $186,000.

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Creative Strategy Lead, Performance Marketing
jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About the Role

Suno is changing who gets to make music, and this role helps bring that to millions of new people. As Creative Strategy Lead, you'll own the creative strategy behind our performance marketing: which audiences we reach, what resonates with each, and how every ad makes us smarter. You'll lead a team of creative specialists, work hand-in-hand with paid media, data science, and production, and build the playbook for how we grow, with full autonomy to shape it.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/wSfvXxWs5tF0RkeL

What You’ll Do

  • Own creative strategy for performance marketing across paid social and beyond, from persona strategy to the creative roadmap and the testing plan behind it

  • Build a persona playbook that spells out what to say, show, and test for each audience, and keep it current as results come in

  • Run the loop from creative analysis to insight to strategy, partnering with paid media and data science on tagging, testing, and reading what drove performance

  • Drive audience research, customer conversations, and competitive intel to deepen our understanding of who we bring in, scale what works, and find new audiences worth reaching

  • Lead and develop a team of creative specialists across UGC, AI, and brand creative, and manage our UGC agency partner

  • Feed what you learn about our users back into product and go-to-market, and help bring millions of new people into creative entertainment

What You’ll Need

  • 8+ years in creative strategy, with deep roots in performance marketing

  • A track record of paid social creative strategy that drove subscriptions and conversions (not brand or awareness campaigns), with results you can speak to

  • Experience at large, complex consumer companies with a wide range of audiences, selling everything from low-price subscriptions to higher-ticket plans

  • Experience leading creative strategists and creatives while acting as the bridge between creative and paid media teams

  • A sharp, clear communicator who can explain exactly how a strategy is built and why

  • Relentlessly proactive: you go looking for the audience insight nobody handed you, and you care deeply about the people you're advertising to

  • Bonus: YouTube or Google display creative, ASO, or lifecycle marketing experience

Additional Notes

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This role requires working onsite at one of our offices.

 

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Compensation

$150,000–$200,000 base salary (before equity)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

About the Role

If you’ve spent your career building world-class support organizations and you’re itching to rebuild one from the ground up — AI-first, data-driven, and at real scale — this is the role. As Director of Customer Experience (Support) at Suno, you’ll own our customer support function end-to-end: setting and managing SLAs, running a lean P&L, and ensuring every user who needs help gets a high-quality experience. You’ll lead a team of 6–8 support ICs and partner closely with Trust & Safety, Product, Billing, Legal, and Policy to solve some of our hardest customer-facing problems. You’ll report to the Sr. Director of Customer Experience & Safety.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/m58ZXW9Sn5TenL7C

What You’ll Do

  • Define, track, and manage to SLAs across all support channels — using data to surface trends, identify gaps, and drive continuous improvement in resolution time and quality.

  • Own the support P&L, managing costs while scaling capacity intelligently as the product and user base grow.

  • Design the right support experience for each problem type — deciding when a user needs a human, an AI agent, a help article, or a proactive fix upstream in the product.

  • Build and iterate on operational processes that make the team faster, more consistent, and less reliant on manual effort — including launching new support channels.

  • Lead and develop a team of 6–8 support ICs, setting clear expectations, coaching on quality, and building a culture that’s as data-minded as it is customer-obsessed.

  • Partner with Product, T&S, Billing, and Legal to close the loop between support signals and product decisions — helping Suno build toward a future where creative fulfillment is a daily reality for everyone.

What You’ll Need

Must-Haves

  • 7–9 years of experience in support leadership, with a track record of building and managing high-performing teams.

  • Background in consumer technology — you understand what it means to support a large, diverse user base with high expectations and low tolerance for friction.

  • Experience building or scaling multi-channel support operations (email, chat, in-app, etc.).

  • A genuinely data-driven operating style — you set goals in metrics, track them rigorously, and use data to make decisions, not just report outcomes.

  • Experience managing a support P&L or cost-per-ticket model.

  • Strong process instincts — you document, systematize, and build for repeatability.

  • Experience with AI-native or AI-assisted support tooling (deflection flows, chatbots, copilots for agents, or similar).

Nice-to-Haves

  • Hands-on experience building with LLM-powered support tools — prompt design, workflow automation, or agent evaluation.

  • Familiarity with Trust & Safety-adjacent support workflows.

  • Background in the music industry or a music-adjacent platforms, whether working with artists, labels, or music creators, with the ability to speak fluently about music production, audio editing, and/or the creative process

  • Experience scaling a support org through rapid company or product growth.

  • Hands-on work operating tiered support models across distinct customer segments, including free and paid subscribers, enterprise or API clients, and high-profile creators or artists, with a strong sense of when and how to escalate and how to calibrate the experience for each tier

  • Background supporting billing, fraud, or identity-related user issues.

  • Experience running community or self-serve support programs (help centers, forums, FAQs).

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from the designated Suno office 5 days a week, per Suno’s company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Willingness to travel (up to 10%) to collaborate with team members across Suno office locations.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.title: Director, Trust & Safety
jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

The role

You will lead Trust & Safety at Suno. Directly leading enforcement operations and policy, you will also partner with PM, Eng, and Legal to scale detection and remediation of violative content, fraud, bots, and identity issues, while also navigating music rights and our regulatory obligations. Generation volume grows faster than any human review model can, so we focus on building enforcement systems that scale with the platform, hold it to a high degree of accuracy, and know exactly what decisions costs. You will report to the Head of Operations and partner regularly with Comms, Product, Engineering, ML, and Legal.

Listen to the song we made about the role: https://suno.com/s/QawvJRO3jhDr1Cb8

What you'll do

  • Build and lead the T&S team, including enforcement operations, policy, vendor programs, quality management, and training.

  • Own enforcement economics end-to-end: cost per decision, precision and recall tradeoffs at volume, automation rate targets, queue design, and the vendor versus in-house mix.

  • Govern AI-assisted decisioning: model-assisted enforcement pipelines, human-in-the-loop thresholds, appeals architecture, and audit accountability for automated actions.

  • Own the BPO relationship and every Trust & Safety vendor partnership: selection, contract negotiation support, capacity strategy, quality accountability, and the decision of what stays outsourced versus moves in-house

  • Run the operational layer of music rights enforcement: rights-matching abuse patterns, impersonation and copyright workflows, in close partnership with Legal.

  • Partner with Legal to translate regulatory regimes (DSA, OSA and emerging AI-content rules) into tooling, process and measurable operational readiness.

  • Represent Trust & Safety to executive leadership with clear metrics and honest tradeoffs.

What you'll bring

  • 8+ years in trust & safety, integrity, or content operations, including 4+ years leading teams through significant scale inflections.

  • Demonstrated ownership of enforcement metrics at a UGC or generative AI platform: automation rate, decision accuracy, cost per action, appeal overturn rate.

  • Experience building or governing model-assisted enforcement with human-in-the-loop design and audit accountability.

  • A track record of moving Product, Engineering, Legal, and Policy without direct authority.

Nice to have

  • Music, media or IP-adjacent platform experience and fluency in rights-matching abuse patterns.

  • Direct exposure to DSA, OSA or emerging AI-content regulatory regimes as operational requirements.

Compensation and benefits

The annual salary range for this role is $195,200 - $256,200 + target equity + benefits (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the Role

If you’re the kind of engineering leader who’d rather ship than spectate, this one’s for you. You’ll lead a team building core product and platform capabilities for over 100 million creators — shaping system design, driving execution, and partnering with product, design, and data science to deliver experiences people actually love. This is a hands-on leadership role: you’ll set technical direction, grow your team, and keep things moving in a fast-paced, music-obsessed environment.

Check out the Suno version of this role here: https://suno.com/s/H3GzRpa6Ze9A6DKr

What You’ll Do

  • Own the technical direction for your team’s domain, driving architecture decisions and ensuring scalable, high-quality systems that serve millions of creators

  • Build, coach, and grow a team of engineers — hiring strong talent, running effective performance cycles, and creating a culture where people do their best work

  • Partner with product management, design, and data science to define roadmaps, scope projects, and ship features that move the needle

  • Navigate the full development lifecycle from ideation through launch, managing tradeoffs and removing blockers so your team stays focused and shipping

  • Champion engineering craft across your team — code quality, robust testing, and the right balance of rapid iteration with long-term maintainability

  • Contribute to Suno’s mission of making creative fulfillment a daily reality for everyone by delivering the tools and platform that turn imagination into music

What You’ll Need

Must-Haves

  • 5–7 years managing a software engineering team, with a track record of shipping impactful consumer products

  • Strong technical foundation — you can review code, guide architectural decisions, and jump into the codebase when needed

  • Experience translating ambiguous problems into clear plans and shipped features alongside product, design, and data science partners

  • A demonstrated ability to hire, develop, and retain strong engineers — you care deeply about growing people’s careers

  • Hands-on experience building and operating systems at scale in a production environment

jobs.title: Graphic Designer, Performance Marketing (Contractor)
jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About the Role

Suno is growing fast, and paid social creative is a major driver of that growth. The right person for this role takes Suno's brand identity and pushes it into performance creative that earns attention and converts – work that drives growth and brings the excitement of using Suno to everyone who sees it.

As Graphic Designer on the Performance Marketing team, you'll own the branded paid social creative pipeline: conceiving, producing, and iterating on work across branded static formats. You'll work closely with the performance marketing team, treating data and channel insights as creative inputs rather than afterthoughts. Over time, you'll help build the workflows and systems that let us scale without losing what makes Suno's creative distinctive. As the team grows, there's a path to managing other creative contributors.

Check out the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/dDrWV7XNe6I5mJax

What You'll Do

  • Translate Suno's brand identity and creative DNA into paid social creative that drives growth across paid channels (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, etc.)

  • Own the full branded creative pipeline – concepting, producing, and iterating on branded static assets

  • Build and maintain a creative roadmap: what to make, what to test, what to push further, and what to move on from

  • Partner with the performance marketing team to use data and channel feedback as creative inputs, not just outputs

  • Use AI tools to extend creative output beyond what's manually possible – and help build the processes and guardrails that keep AI-assisted work on-brand and up to Suno's standards

  • Develop workflows and production processes that scale creative output without diluting brand quality

  • Help shape how the next generation of creators discovers Suno – the creative you make is often their first impression



What You'll Need

  • 4-6 years in performance creative, paid social design, or growth-focused creative at a consumer tech, DTC, or growth-stage company

  • Expert graphic design skills: strong static design fundamentals and a sharp eye for details and consumer psychology

  • Portfolio of paid social work that demonstrates both craft and a performance orientation

  • Expert-level proficiency in Figma, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, etc.

  • Fluency in what makes paid social creative work: hooks, formats, platform conventions, and what drives meaningful iteration

  • Ability to internalize a brand's visual identity and push it into new formats without losing what makes it distinctive

Compensation

$75 - $90 per hour

Additional Notes

20-40 hours per week

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About the role

The Lead Corporate Security Engineer will be our domain expert for securing our Corporate IT environment. You’ll work closely with colleagues in IT, Business Systems, Security, and Engineering to ensure that our corporate systems are implemented and maintained securely. As a senior member of the team, your impact will be split between building your team, enabling others, and doing hands-on work to mature our systems, processes, and behaviors.

You'll lead the corporate security domain end to end: identity and access governance, endpoint and vulnerability management, detection and response, third-party integration risk, vendor assessment, and SaaS posture. You'll set the standard, own the roadmap, and be accountable for the outcome. IT Engineering runs the platforms day to day and are your closest partners.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/BiNdRVfLZRJXlfSW

How this role works with IT

Ownership splits by layer, not by system. IT Engineering owns the run; you own the standard and the direction.

  • You set the corporate security roadmap. What we secure, in what order, to what bar with buy-in from leadership and XFN stakeholders

  • IT engineering owns platform operations. Our SaaS portfolio is administered and integrated by them. You define what those platforms must enforce

  • You raise the bar around you. You make your reasoning explicit so that partners make good security calls without you in the room, and you build the tooling and defaults that make the secure path the default path

What you'll own

Identity and access governance

  • Own the access model at Suno: the RBAC and entitlement design, least-privilege defaults, and the governance layer in Lumos that enforces them

  • Set the standard for what access review, certification, and approval should look like here — then build toward it rather than importing someone else's framework

  • Drive access lifecycle automation so joiner/mover/leaver is correct by default and exceptions are visible

  • Get ahead of non-human identity: service accounts, agents, and automations are a growing share of what holds access at Suno, and we need a model for them before it's urgent

Endpoint security and vulnerability management

  • Own the security standard for our fleet: hardening baseline, compliance signals, device trust, and how endpoint posture feeds access decisions

  • Own third-party vulnerability management as a program — coverage, risk-based remediation SLAs, reporting, and the negotiation with teams whose tools are the problem

  • Partner with the IT engineer who owns Kandji so the standard becomes deployed policy without degrading how people work

Detection and response

  • Own our EDR deployment and maintenance

  • Collaborate with Detection and Response on corporate security incidents to closure

Third-party and integration risk

  • Own how Suno evaluates third-party access: integration and OAuth review for Slack, Google Workspace and the rest of the portfolio, plus vendor security assessment at purchase and renewal

  • Define our risk appetite in practice and make it legible enough that others apply it without you

  • Turn recurring decisions into policy, scope guidance, and tooling so the review queue shrinks as the company grows

SaaS security posture

  • Build and own the program: the bar for our SaaS applications, the assessment cadence, and the remediation that follows

  • Improve tenant-level configuration across the portfolio — SSO and SCIM coverage, MFA and session policy, admin role hygiene, OAuth grant and token management, data sharing defaults

Cross-functional leadership

  • Work with IT, Security, Engineering, AI Enablement, and Legal to shape how Suno builds and buys

  • Influence the scope of what comes next: how our GRC function plugs in, what we automate versus staff, where the next investment goes

  • Mentor and raise the technical bar for people around you, including partners who aren't security specialists

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: you've formed your own view of our security posture, built working relationships with the IT engineers the broader Security team, and told us the three things we're wrong about

  • First 6 months: a corporate security roadmap exists that IT and the CISO are aligned behind, with the sequencing and the tradeoffs made explicit; the highest-risk items are already moving

  • First year: entitlement sprawl and vulnerability backlog are measurably down, detection reflects our real risks, third-party review is fast enough that nobody routes around it, and the standard holds because it's built into tooling and shared judgment rather than into you

What you'll bring

  • ~8+ years in corporate/enterprise security or security engineering, including having owned identity, endpoint, or SaaS security as a domain rather than as a set of tickets

  • Deep hands-on expertise with a modern IdP and with IGA or access-governance tooling (Lumos, Veza, ConductorOne, Opal, or similar)

  • You've designed an entitlement or RBAC model across a large SaaS portfolio and lived with the consequences long enough to know what breaks

  • Endpoint security depth in a macOS-primary fleet: MDM-delivered hardening, compliance and device trust, third-party patch and vulnerability management at scale

  • Strong command of OAuth, SAML, OIDC, and SCIM, and of the risk model behind third-party integrations

  • A track record of setting a security standard that other people applied without you enforcing it — written policy, tooling, defaults, or all three

  • Experience influencing engineering and business teams who don't report to you, early enough in their process to change the outcome

  • Automation fluency: Python or TypeScript, REST APIs, and a habit of building integrations and internal tooling as a normal part of the job

  • Excellent writing and judgment under ambiguity. You can hold a position with an executive and change it when the evidence says to

  • A calibrated sense of risk and how to communicate likelihood, impact, and tradeoffs

Helpful, not required: insider risk or DLP programs, zero-trust network access, SOC 2 or ISO program ownership, just-in-time access patterns or identity-as-code, securing AI agent and non-human identity access, prior experience as the first or second security hire at a fast-growing company.

Work Location Policy

This role is expected to work from Suno's NYC or Cambridge, MA office 5 days a week, per Suno's company policy. Full-time employees will receive competitive equity packages, and comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered may vary depending on location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Additional Notes

Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Willingness to travel (up to 25%) to lead team members and support offices across Suno locations, with a deliberate cadence in Cambridge and NYC during the first six months.

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

jobs.description_html:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

About the Role

The Manager, Music Marketing is a mid-level role responsible for working within the team that shapes how the world discovers, experiences, creates and connects with music on Suno.

The ideal candidate is a creative marketer who understands how audiences are discovering and engaging with music online and IRL. You’ll be part of the artist & music marketing team that shapes the marketing programs we’re creating in partnership with the industry. You’ll also be responsible for the ideation and execution of the marketing campaigns that help fans connect with the music and artists on Suno.

This role reports to the Head of Artist Marketing & Editorial and sits across music, marketing, product, and the Suno brand, making it a uniquely high-impact seat at a company redefining what music creation can be.

Listen to the song we made about the role! https://suno.com/s/oinhIznaWyP1bo3W

What You’ll Do

  • Own the overall strategy and performance of artist marketing campaigns, ensuring consistent pipeline, quality execution, and measurable impact

  • Own the A to Z of a campaign ensuring that it’s a success for the artist, the fans, and Suno

  • Make cool things happen for artists who are making music with Suno

  • Make cool things happen for artists delivering their music on Suno to be remixed and interacted with

  • Challenge and help define what artist and music marketing looks like at a music creation and music interaction platform - we are not a DSP and we are not a label

  • Work with the marketing, editorial, comms, creative and brand teams to find and build the pipelines and programs that support artists, creative community, and the industry

  • Work cross-functionally with the growth, product and brand teams to represent the artist community in product launches

  • Create new opportunities (on and off platform) for music and artists on Suno

  • Serve as an escalation point and senior relationship holder for high-priority industry and artist partnerships and their representatives

  • Establish and maintain best practices around campaign operations, including data analysis, rights clearances, contracting, cross-functional coordination, and performance reporting

  • Partner with Legal and Finance to ensure all artist agreements and payments are handled with rigor and care

  • Collaborate within the artist & music marketing team to disrupt and redefine what artist marketing and music consumptions looks like in 2026 and beyond

  • Own success and metrics reporting, including campaign performance, reach, and remix metrics

What You’ll Need

Required Experience & Expertise

  • 8-10 years of experience having worked in the music and entertainment industries, preferably from a DSP, management or record label.

  • Experience working with talent is a must, with a deep sensitivity and empathy to working with artists and handling their creative projects and outputs

  • A creative brain

  • You’re a builder and maker, not just a facilitator

  • Deep familiarity with music industry structures including recording, publishing, and representation agreements, and how they affect partnership and campaign execution

  • Experience ideating, executing and managing end-to-end artist marketing campaigns with cross-functional stakeholders and complex logistics

  • Relationships with artists, managers, and various stakeholders in the music industry

  • Excellent communicator: able to represent Suno credibly with senior artist teams and external partners, and communicate clearly and directly internally

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and energized by the pace and possibility of a high-growth environment

  • Passion for music and sincere belief in technology's potential to expand creative access and expression

  • A thirst for music culture

Preferred

  • Experience at a music technology, streaming, or AI company

  • Experience working within or alongside product and engineering teams

Additional Notes:

  • Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

  • This role requires working on-site in Los Angeles (Venice Beach).

Compensation:

The annual salary range for this role is $160,000 – $210,000

Perks & Benefits for Full-Time Employees:

  • Company Equity Package

  • 401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)

  • Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)

  • 11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time

  • 16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave

  • Creative Education Stipend

  • Generous Commuter Allowance

  • In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

Suno is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis under provincial, federal, state, and local laws, regulations, or ordinances. We will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of state and local laws, including the Massachusetts Fair Chance in Employment Act, NYC Fair Chance Act, LA City Fair Chance Ordinance, and San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Founded in 2023 by Harvard alumni with a shared passion for music, Suno has quickly grown to 250 employees while empowering more than 100 million people to create original songs. In 2026, we raised a $400 million Series D at a $5.4 billion valuation to continue building innovative products that amplify creativity and imagination.

 

About the Role

Suno is growing fast, and paid social creative is a major driver of that growth. The right person for this role takes Suno's brand identity and pushes it into performance creative that earns attention and converts – work that drives growth and brings the excitement of using Suno to everyone who sees it.

As Graphic Designer on the Performance Marketing team, you'll own the branded paid social creative pipeline: conceiving, producing, and iterating on work across branded static formats. You'll work closely with the performance marketing team, treating data and channel insights as creative inputs rather than afterthoughts. Over time, you'll help build the workflows and systems that let us scale without losing what makes Suno's creative distinctive. As the team grows, there's a path to managing other creative contributors.

 

Check out the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/dDrWV7XNe6I5mJax

 

What You'll Do

  • Translate Suno's brand identity and creative DNA into paid social creative that drives growth across paid channels (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, etc.)

  • Own the full branded creative pipeline – concepting, producing, and iterating on branded static assets

  • Build and maintain a creative roadmap: what to make, what to test, what to push further, and what to move on from

  • Partner with the performance marketing team to use data and channel feedback as creative inputs, not just outputs

  • Use AI tools to extend creative output beyond what's manually possible – and help build the processes and guardrails that keep AI-assisted work on-brand and up to Suno's standards

  • Develop workflows and production processes that scale creative output without diluting brand quality

  • Help shape how the next generation of creators discovers Suno – the creative you make is often their first impression



What You'll Need

  • 4-6 years in performance creative, paid social design, or growth-focused creative at a consumer tech, DTC, or growth-stage company

  • Expert graphic design skills: strong static design fundamentals and a sharp eye for details and consumer psychology

  • Portfolio of paid social work that demonstrates both craft and a performance orientation

  • Expert-level proficiency in Figma, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator, etc.

  • Fluency in what makes paid social creative work: hooks, formats, platform conventions, and what drives meaningful iteration

  • Ability to internalize a brand's visual identity and push it into new formats without losing what makes it distinctive

 

Compensation

$75 - $90 per hour

 

Additional Notes

20-40 hours per week
